conclusion: Aligning HOIPrior's inference protocol with the protocol its baselines were measured under closes the recorded contact gap. Guided, the sealed D2-X checkpoint reaches statistical contact parity with the guided released model: Arm A minus a0-old has contact recall -0.0043, precision +0.0114, F1 +0.0035 and contact_percent -0.0120, all four with CIs crossing zero, and Arm B's F1 difference -0.0007 also crosses zero. The gain is geometric, not a shift of operating point: the paired GT-contact-frame distance moves -1.4371 cm [-1.7204, -1.1532], the median goes 3.1835 -> 1.7178 cm, the [0,2) cm mass rises 0.359 -> 0.547, and on the unthresholded residual Arm A is indistinguishable from the guided released model (+0.2216 cm, CI crosses zero). Arm A is the preregistered primary and has the highest contact F1 (0.73071), but Arm B is the configuration that survives cost scrutiny: about 88% of the recall gain, 96% of the F1 gain and 85% of the distance gain, with an object-translation ratio of 1.0063 and foot sliding IMPROVED at 0.9797. P2 preregistered mandatory cost reporting but no cost threshold; reported only for comparability, if D2-Q0's <=1.10 bar were applied Arm A would fail foot sliding (CI upper 1.1661) and clear object translation by 1.7e-4, while Arm B would clear both. D2-Q0's negative is overturned: it omitted the feet-floor term entirely and measured on a checkpoint with 95.3 cm object-goal error. The pre-run prediction that Arm A would saturate position_outside_rate and degenerate is FALSIFIED - every run has nonfinite_values 0 and position_outside_rate 0.0. What guidance does not fix: Arm A's >=8 cm tail is still fatter than the released model's (0.1272 vs 0.1052) and object-trajectory and penetration costs remain against a0-old, consistent with the 0.83 cm genuine generative-geometry gap. This is protocol alignment, not a model improvement: it changes how HOIPrior is sampled, not the quality of the prior.

Mechanism, from data/train/norm.npy (1 normalised unit = 3.32917 / 1.09975 / 3.48764 m): the 12-element metric MSE at code/priors/losses.py:156 makes a hand joint displaced by e metres cost the author 4.167e^2 and us 0.031e^2 once the shared weight-1 joint_position channel is counted, an effective 135.2x under-weighting (140.06x on raw weights), so an 8 cm hand miss costs the author 0.0267 and us 0.00020; and because the author uses smooth_l1 for the object surface (code/models/infbagel.py:861) where we use MSE (losses.py:196), the object term is under-weighted 52.4x (104.77x raw, halved by the smooth_l1 1/2 coefficient) on exactly the quantity behind end_obj_trans_err and xy_points_err. This matches the measured geometry: pooled gross-miss (GT-contact frame with the hand >= 8 cm from the object) is 0.1216 under D2-X + P2 Arm B against 0.1052 for the released guided row, median hand world error at gross-miss frames is 24.12 cm, and 67.7 percent of those frames have hand error >= 2x pelvis error, i.e. reach error, not body placement. A preregistered pre-flight diagnostic with a fixed abort rule runs first: evaluate the existing non-reportable checkpoint results/p1b-author-diffusion-8x3090-full-r1-s42-20260717/checkpoints/p1b-author-diffusion-8x3090-full-r1-s42-20260717_epoch100.pth (101 x 597,868 = 60,384,668 processed windows, 98.3 percent of D2-X's 61,440,000) on the official 438x3 native protocol to test whether D2-T's collapse at 6,144,000 windows (MPJPE 34.7367, end-object 38.5563, contact F1 0.2764, foot sliding 0.1761) was an undertraining artefact; if that row is not better than D2-X on BOTH xy_points_err (4.050519689917564) AND end_obj_trans_err (3.7402085959911346), formal training is not started and the direction closes as a negative preflight. conclusion: The preregistered D2-AH pre-flight failed its fixed abort rule and the direction closes as a negative preflight. The author's metric geometric recipe at 60,384,668 processed windows, 98.3 percent of the D2-X budget, reads xy_points_err 5.7623 against D2-X 4.050520 (+42.3 percent) and end_obj_trans_err 5.4176 against 3.740209 (+44.8 percent), failing both gates. The preregistered tree-effect control then confirmed the failure rather than excusing it: seven of the eight comparable metrics reproduce the earlier epoch500 row within 1.61 percent relative, but end_obj_trans_err moves +0.3642 cm (+11.0 percent), a real metric-specific tree effect on one of the two gate metrics. Even crediting epoch100 that entire correction leaves it at 5.05 against D2-X 3.7402, while the xy_points_err tree effect of +0.0173 is about 99 times too small to cover a 1.7118 cm shortfall. What this refutes is the affordability of the remedy, not the dimensional diagnosis: at 299,531,868 windows, 4.88 times the formal budget, the same recipe beats D2-X on xy_points_err by 0.8198 cm, contact F1 by 0.0286, contact recall by 0.0493 and hand penetration by 0.0517, and its contact_percent 0.5311 sits closer to the ground truth 0.66188 than D2-X's 0.47655. The epoch100 penetration and foot-sliding advantages are engagement artefacts: its contact_percent is 0.3192 against a ground truth of 0.66188, and its penetration ratios fall to 0.543 and 0.570 of D2-X in proportion, whereas epoch500 raises engagement above D2-X and lowers hand penetration at the same time. Separately, and reprioritising the remaining work: on end_obj_trans_err D2-X (3.7402) is statistically indistinguishable from the author's own from-scratch recipe at 4.88x budget (3.6866, paired CI [-0.3798, 0.2521] crossing zero), so the gap to the released checkpoint (3.0372) is not attributable to the diffusion training recipe; the in-house consistency reproduction reads 3.5553, so distillation accounts for only part of the residual and the rest is unexplained. No formal training was started, no run id was allocated and no checkpoint was produced.

conclusion: P3 completes a 3x2 {checkpoint: D2-X, D2-AG, D2-AE} x {sampler: 500-step unguided, 500-step + P2 Arm B} on the fixed official 438-sequence protocol, one execution tree, five new cells and one sealed cell reused by reference. All three preregistered same-tree hash gates passed bit-exactly, which is a methodological result in its own right: the guidance implementation is empirically inert on the unguided path for three architectures, so the sealed unguided cells stand without substitution and the main effects are interpretable, not just the tree-immune interaction. The preregistered verdict is a COST FAILURE. Penetration closure is met - D2-AG + Arm B reads hand penetration 0.1721393 against the released 0.1624020 (+6.0%, previously +41.3%) and body penetration 2.7465671 against 2.5892666 (+6.1%, previously +40.0%), both inside the preregistered +/-10% band - and PROTECTION (ii) holds (end_obj_trans_err +0.0515 [-0.0091, +0.1178] against the +0.25 cm bar). But contact parity is NOT met (contact_f1 0.6934294 against the 0.7072577 floor) and PROTECTION (i) is violated (-0.0331 [-0.0517, -0.0145] against D2-X + Arm B, lower bound below -0.02). The pre-run additive prediction of contact_f1 0.7391880 is FALSIFIED by -0.0458, exactly where the plan said an interaction would show: the interaction on contact_f1 is -0.0458 [-0.0591, -0.0329] and on contact_recall -0.0592 [-0.0759, -0.0428], both excluding zero, while the interactions on hand penetration, body penetration, foot sliding and end-object all cross zero. The mechanism is a monotone dose-response the declared second arm was built to expose: the guidance gain on contact_f1 is +0.0891 on D2-X, +0.0683 on D2-AE and +0.0433 on D2-AG, and D2-AE's interaction (-0.0208 [-0.0359, -0.0057]) is about half D2-AG's. The sparse relation field damps guidance's contact effect and making its source self-conditioned damps it about twice as much. This retroactively vindicates part of P2's reason for excluding D2-AG - not as a safety issue, since non-finite values and out-of-range positions are zero everywhere, but as an efficacy one; the P3 overturn of that exclusion was correct on safety and wrong on efficacy, and neither record is rewritten. The pre-committed artefact narrative did NOT materialise: in the unguided cells engagement is essentially identical (contact_percent 0.4766 / 0.4771 / 0.4766) while hand penetration is 0.2454 / 0.1837 / 0.1794 and hand_pen_ratio 0.1439 / 0.1129 / 0.1216, so the relation field's penetration advantage is not bought with engagement. The declared second arm is reported as declared and not elevated: D2-AE + Arm B against D2-X + Arm B has contact_f1 -0.0163 [-0.0342, +0.0016] (crosses zero, contact statistically intact), hand penetration -0.0483 [-0.0827, -0.0161], body penetration -0.7495 [-1.2884, -0.2482], but foot sliding +0.0411 [+0.0218, +0.0604] and end-object +0.4521 [+0.2309, +0.6774], with penetration gaps to released of +11.5% and +11.1%, just outside the band D2-AG cleared. Neither arm dominates. The synthesis is that inference guidance and the sparse relation field are partially redundant on contact - both push the hand toward the object, so their contact gains do not stack - and complementary on penetration, which guidance barely moves (D2-X 0.2454 -> 0.2294, D2-AG 0.1837 -> 0.1721). Nothing was trained, no checkpoint was selected or produced, the evaluator and the fixed native D2 protocol are unchanged, guidance remains default-off, and the D2-AG and D2-AE negative classifications stand.
next_action: Record P3 as a preregistered cost failure and stop this direction. Do not read the penetration closure as a headline result and do not use either guided arm as a checkpoint-selection signal: D2-AG remains selfcond-relation-source-transfer-negative-stop and D2-AE remains sparse-relation-field-transfer-negative-stop, neither is selectable as a prior initializer, guidance stays default-off, and Phase 1B HOIPrior search stays closed. The transferable finding for any later contact work is the redundancy structure: mechanisms that move the hand toward the object at sampling time do not stack with each other, while penetration and contact respond to different levers. The next-session entry point is unchanged: a dated Phase 1C HSIPrior plan-only preregistration on phase/01c-hsi, trained from random initialization. Any production use of guidance, any stepwise object requery, and any new direction still require a separate dated plan amendment and explicit user approval.

hypothesis: Every one of the nine D2 HOIPrior configurations reaches its held-out validation minimum at 21,504,000 or 24,576,000 processed windows and then degrades monotonically to the sealed 61,440,000-window budget (total +5.6..+12.4%, contact term +25.4..+30.6%), so the fixed 61.44M budget is an uncontrolled shared constant at roughly 2.5x past every model's validation optimum, and all ten configurations were compared with each other at that common over-trained point. Because a denoising validation loss and sampled-motion metrics can decouple in a diffusion model, whether this has any consequence in metric space is unknown and has never been measured. This experiment evaluates six existing D2-X cadence checkpoints (3.072M, 12.288M, 21.504M, 24.576M, 43.008M, 61.44M) under the frozen official native protocol and tests one preregistered comparison: paired sequence-level bootstrap of contact_f1 at C3=21.504M versus C6=61.44M. A lower CI bound above zero means the overfitting has reached metric space and refutes the increase-the-budget direction; a CI crossing zero means the two decouple and leaves that direction open with this curve as its baseline. C3 was fixed as the single comparison point from the mode of the nine contact argmins (7/9 at 21.50M) after seeing the loss curves but before seeing any native metric, and may not be changed afterwards.

P4 established that end_obj_trans_err and xy_points_err are GOAL-RECALL metrics (the object goal handed to the model IS GT object translation at the exact scored frame, 0.0574 cm over all 438 sequences; pelvis_goal equals GT pelvis at frame 15 to 0.0000 cm while the metric scores frame 14), so our gaps there are constraint-satisfaction deficits. D2-AJ splits the pathway into separate pelvis (xz), object and progress tokens (+525,312 params, 4->6 condition tokens, position 20->22, architecture_variant d2aj_split_goal_tokens), same budget and every other setting as D2-AI. PRIOR STATED HONESTLY: this is MORE LIKELY INERT THAN NOT - the fused Linear(12,512) is already an affine map of the same information and the split is close to a reparameterization at the first layer; any gain must come from attention weighting the two goals separately per head and frame. Evidence-index conclusion 9 (contact levers do not stack, absorbed as a generic residual) applies the same absorption risk here, and D2-AE is the cautionary precedent (all five internal causal gates passed with well-separated CIs, native transfer still null).

hypothesis: P5's contact-mask threshold sweep returned a preregistered null (contact_recall +0.0000240 for 0.95 -> 0.25), falsifying 'the mask gate limits guidance's action surface'. A verified decomposition of the real guided path (reconciliation exact, 72/72 checks, max abs err 0.0, 8 sequences via monkeypatched evaluator) relocates the constraint INSIDE the author's hand term bs*(loss_contact + loss_consistency) (guidance_loss.py:69). The two sub-terms respond to mask width in OPPOSITE directions: loss_contact 0.02117535 -> 0.02125364 (+0.000078, UP) while loss_consistency 1.39546636 -> 1.39422995 (-0.001236, DOWN); net DOWN, ratio 15.79x measured vs 15.58x closed form on the 6/36 steps where the mask changed. Cause is a normalization dimension mismatch: loss_contact is an L1 mean over bs*T*2 slots (linear in admitted frames k) while loss_consistency masks a T x T outer product (quadratic in k), so 4k*s_bar/(T*(d-0.02)) grows with k and a wider mask over-cancels harder -- no threshold can fix it. loss_consistency is 98.5% of the hand term, loss_contact 1.5% by value but 29.2% of gradient norm. P6 therefore manipulates the two sub-term WEIGHTS and the consistency normalizer, not the mask.

hypothesis: P8-P9c tuned the DOSE of the hand-object geometry term (weight 50 -> 3) but never audited the FORMULA. masked_hand_object_distance_loss (code/priors/losses.py:40-91) drives palm-joint-to-predicted-object-surface distance to ZERO via nearest.square() (:87), whereas the author's inference guidance whose palm indices P8 copied (code/guidance_loss.py:15-16) uses a 2 cm hinge, maximum(dists - 0.02, 0) (code/guidance_loss.py:36-39), whose gradient is exactly zero below 2 cm. The palm joint is INTERIOR to the hand mesh while hand_pen_loss_omomo scores hand VERTEX penetration, so driving joint-to-surface distance to 0 forces the surrounding vertices inside the object. Second, the term does not detach the object surface (losses.py:75, fed predicted_surface from :265-267), so it can reduce itself by moving the OBJECT toward the hand rather than the hand toward the object; the author's consistency term DOES detach the object (guidance_loss.py:42-47) and only the hinge term does not, and P6 already measured that pathway's magnitude on the guidance side (object grad L2: translation 2.678, rotation 5.252). These two mechanisms separately and precisely predict W3's two regressions vs the no-geometry baseline H0/D2-AI: hand_pen_loss_omomo 0.16451 -> 0.25874 (+57%), human_pen_loss_infbagel 2.59925 -> 4.07788 (+57%), end_obj_trans_err 3.89162 -> 4.68200 (+0.790 cm). P10 repairs the formula at fixed dose (weight 3.0).

retracted_mask_expansion_probe.status: RETRACTED. Asserted earlier in this phase and possibly cited in earlier drafts of this record.
retracted_mask_expansion_probe.what_was_claimed: on real decoded D2-AI contact the author-visible mask expands from 1000 frames at threshold 0.95 to 1368 frames at 0.25, +36.8%, with 18% of probed frames lying in the newly opened (0.25, 0.95] band.
retracted_mask_expansion_probe.why_it_is_wrong: that probe did not measure the tensor guidance actually consumes. It measured decoded contact outside the guided reverse loop, not the contact channels present at the guided steps. The +36.8% and 18% figures are withdrawn and must not be cited.
retracted_mask_expansion_probe.replacement_measurement: a verified decomposition on the REAL guided path shows the 0.95 -> 0.25 sweep opens only 6 of 7200 channel elements at the guided steps, i.e. 0.083%.
retracted_mask_expansion_probe.why_so_small: the predicted contact logits are near-saturated and bimodal at the guided steps: 43.67% of elements are already above 0.95 and 43.75% are above 0.25, so almost nothing lies in the band between. Arm B guides only the last 10 reverse steps, where x0_hat is nearly clean and the contact predictions have already binarized. There is very little mass left for a threshold to reclassify.
retracted_mask_expansion_probe.consequence: the null is over-determined. The mask does not merely fail to help -- at the guided steps it barely changes at all, because the threshold operates on a distribution that has already collapsed to its endpoints.

guided_path_decomposition.provenance: measured on 8 sequences via a monkeypatched real evaluator run on the guided path. Reconciliation against the unpatched path was exact: 72/72 checks, max abs err 0.0.

author_hand_term_split_0_95_to_0_25.net: DOWN -- loss_consistency dominates the sum, so widening the mask lowers the hand term overall even though the contact sub-term rises.

ratio_on_steps_where_the_mask_actually_c.reading: the measured |dloss_consistency| / |dloss_contact| ratio agrees with the closed-form prediction, so the cancellation is understood analytically and not merely observed.

guided_path_decomposition.cause_of_the_over_cancellation: loss_contact is an L1 mean over bs*T*2 slots, so one newly admitted frame adds (d - 0.02) / (2*bs*T) -- LINEAR in the number of admitted frames k. loss_consistency masks a T x T outer product, so one newly admitted frame lights ~2k pairs and subtracts 2k*s_bar / (bs*T*T) -- QUADRATIC in k. The ratio is 4k*s_bar / (T*(d - 0.02)), which GROWS with k. A wider mask therefore over-cancels harder: every frame the threshold admits adds a little contact pull and subtracts proportionally more consistency penalty. No choice of threshold fixes this, because the pathology is in the relative scaling of the two sub-terms, not in where the cut is placed.

sub_term_shares.reading: loss_contact is 1.5% of the hand term by value but 29.2% of the total gradient norm, so it is not negligible in the update -- it is simply outvoted in the loss by a consistency term that moves the other way.

clamp_is_not_binding.reading: 0.0538% of update elements saturate at clamp=1.0, so the clamp is not truncating the mask's effect and cannot be blamed for the null.

direction_is_unchanged.reading: the guidance gradient points in essentially the same direction at 0.95 and at 0.25. The threshold does not redirect guidance; it barely rescales it.

guided_path_decomposition.mechanism_of_the_null: three independent measurements converge. (1) At the guided steps only 0.083% of channel elements change, because contact predictions have already binarized by the last 10 reverse steps. (2) Of that small change, the contact sub-term's gain is over-cancelled ~15.8x by the consistency sub-term, an effect that grows with mask width by construction. (3) The resulting gradient is 0.9977-cosine-identical in direction and the clamp is not binding. The mask threshold is therefore not a lever on this path at all, and the failure is structural rather than a matter of tuning.

results.select_confirm_split_why_not: the split existed solely to keep threshold selection honest. The dose-response is numerically flat -- the four sub-0.95 cells agree with each other to full float precision on every contact aggregate and differ from A0 only at the ~1e-5 level -- so NO threshold was selected and the PRIMARY test on half B was never run.

hypothesis: After P5 falsified the mask-gate inference, the constraint was relocated INSIDE the author's hand term bs*(loss_contact + loss_consistency) (guidance_loss.py:69): loss_consistency is 98.5% of the hand term by value but only 1.5% is loss_contact, which nonetheless carries 29.2% of the gradient norm, and the two sub-terms respond to mask width in opposite directions. P6 therefore manipulates the two sub-term weights and the consistency normalizer rather than the mask, plus a non-deployable ground-truth-mask cell U bounding what a perfect engagement decision could recover. Full hypothesis text is retained on the preregistration row p1-hoi-p6-guidance-subterm-reweight-preregister-s42-20260804.

cell_u_outcome_defect_disclosure_2026082.what_this_reopens: the inference-time contact-mask direction is NOT closed on this evidence, and the attribution of the residual ~82.66% engagement gap to a TRAINING-side geometry property is unsupported
cell_u_outcome_defect_disclosure_2026082.why_void_rather_than_merely_weakened: the degenerate mask is OVER-BROAD, and an over-broad contact mask applies contact guidance on frames ground truth says are not in contact, which is a sufficient mechanism for damaging precision. The sealed finding was that the GT mask made contact_f1 significantly WORSE. Had the finding been that the mask helped, over-broadness would only have understated the help and the finding would survive a fortiori. Because the finding is 'it hurt', and over-broadness is a mechanism that hurts, the two are confounded and cannot be separated. The probe never implemented a perfect engagement decision on 2 of its 3 windows, so it never measured what it claims to bound.

hypothesis: Preregistered Phase 1B P7: inference-time object-goal terminal guidance term. The author's guidance knows only 'the palm should touch the object'; it has no notion of where the object should END UP. Adds a deployable terminal-frame term weighted by object_goal_weight, on top of the P6 winner (contact_weight=3). object_goal is a task INPUT available at inference time (not ground truth), so unlike cell U this IS deployable.

config.kind: inference-only object-goal terminal guidance sweep on top of the P6 winner; no training, no checkpoint, no evaluator change
config.frame_convention_note: The codec decodes object_translation in GLOBAL coordinates (window_codec.py:251) while sample_step has already converted object_goal to WINDOW-LOCAL (test_infbagel_hoi.py:415). Differencing them as-is would pull the object toward a meaningless point without raising. The goal is therefore lifted back to global with the decode's own WindowFrame (priors/diffusion.py:513-519), guaranteeing both operands share a frame by construction. Tests include a negative control confirming that a frame mismatch is detectable (tests/test_hoi_guidance_object_goal.py:128-149).

results.winner_headline: confirm-half end_obj_trans_err -0.02824 [-0.06620, -0.00175] cm, significantly improved; obj_trans_dist -0.00391 null, contact_f1 +0.00040 null, mpjpe +0.00451 null. The only clean cell: endpoint improved with no significant degradation anywhere, and the full trajectory moved favourably rather than being traded away.
results.honest_framing: The improvement is 0.028 cm, about 0.7% of 3.91, and leaves a large gap to the released model's 3.037. end_obj_trans_err scores the single frame whose target the model was handed, so optimizing it directly sits close to metric-gaming; this is why obj_trans_dist is reported beside it in every claim, and why the term ships disabled by default (object_goal_weight: 0.0 in code/config/sampler/hoi_prior.yaml).
results.dose_response_summary: G1 (weight 1) is the winner: end_obj significantly improved with no significant degradation. Above weight 1 the endpoint gain stops being significant while mpjpe significantly degrades. G2 (weight 10): end_obj -0.03268 SIG but mpjpe +0.01792 trending degradation. G3/G4 (weight 50/200): end_obj null, mpjpe +0.02552/+0.02867 SIG WORSE, guidance loss 13419/38040 vs G0 5211, gradient RMS 2.677/10.612 vs 0.368. The usable region is narrow: weight 1 is already near saturation.

hypothesis: Preregistered Phase 1B P10: P8-P9c tuned the DOSE of the hand-object geometry term (weight 50 -> 3) but never audited the FORMULA. masked_hand_object_distance_loss (code/priors/losses.py) drives the palm-joint-to-predicted-object-surface distance to ZERO, whereas the author's inference guidance whose palm indices P8 copied uses a 2 cm hinge with exactly zero gradient below 2 cm; and the term does not detach the predicted object surface, so it can reduce itself by moving the OBJECT toward the hand. These two mechanisms were predicted to explain W3's two regressions against the no-geometry baseline H0/D2-AI (hand_pen_loss_omomo +57%, human_pen_loss_infbagel +57%, end_obj_trans_err +0.790 cm). P10 repairs the formula at fixed dose (weight 3.0) as a 2x2. Full hypothesis text is retained on the preregistration row p1-hoi-p10-geometry-term-repair-preregister-s42-20260809.

hypothesis: Preregistered Phase 1B P10: P8-P9c tuned the DOSE of the hand-object geometry term (weight 50 -> 3) but never audited the FORMULA. masked_hand_object_distance_loss (code/priors/losses.py) drives the palm-joint-to-predicted-object-surface distance to ZERO, whereas the author's inference guidance whose palm indices P8 copied uses a 2 cm hinge with exactly zero gradient below 2 cm; and the term does not detach the predicted object surface, so it can reduce itself by moving the OBJECT toward the hand. PROVENANCE: A10/A01 launched at commit 91232ad, but their metrics.json records 5d39ac3. _git_commit() is resolved live at metrics-write time (code/train_hoi_prior.py:6251) and metrics.json is written only at the end of the run, so commits landing mid-run retroactively become that run's recorded provenance. THREE commits landed while A10/A01 were running: 981b9b0 (A11 config, ~18:55, first), b51c3b3 (registry repair) and 5d39ac3 (bootstrap tool); the recorded value is simply the last one. A11 escaped only because AGENTS.md forbids worker source edits mid-run, so the worker was pinned at 981b9b0 - insulation by rule, not by foresight. Verified independently by two sessions: git diff 91232ad..5d39ac3 -- code/ touches exactly one file, config_train_hoi_prior_p10_both.yaml (A11's config), which A10/A01 never load; train_hoi_prior.py, priors/losses.py and their own configs are byte-identical across that range. The executed objective, data and training code are provably those of 91232ad and the 2x2's internal validity is intact, but the record asserts a commit that did not exist at launch. Fix belongs in a later change - resolve the commit at run START and carry it in the record, rather than calling git rev-parse at metrics-write time.

conclusion: NEGATIVE. No cell satisfies PRIMARY, so the classification is geometry-term-repair-negative-stop and no checkpoint is selected. The load-bearing negative is mechanistic: the zero-distance target is NOT the cause of the penetration deficit -- no cell puts hand_pen_loss_omomo or human_pen_loss_infbagel significantly below W3, refuting the mechanism this sub-phase was built on. Only H2 (hinge contact-neutral, contact_percent 0.64230 -> 0.62639) and H4 (detach keeps contact_percent above 0.60) held; H1 was partial and H3 was falsified in the opposite direction by large significant margins (end_obj_trans_err +3.22792 [+2.81104, +3.63130]). The hinge x detach interaction is significant and large on every object/motion metric (end_obj_trans_err -3.59914 [-3.98861, -3.21700], obj_trans_dist -2.99965 [-3.71084, -2.30046], trans_dist -0.53884 [-0.83383, -0.24125], mpjpe -0.52311 [-0.83751, -0.20904], pelvis_goal_error_cm -0.46656 [-0.74537, -0.17982], obj_rot_dist -0.05831 [-0.09722, -0.01959]) and absent on every contact and penetration metric, so neither main effect is interpretable alone: detach alone is catastrophic on object placement while detach+hinge returns end_obj_trans_err to -0.24586 [-0.62987, +0.11190] against W3, i.e. slightly better and not significant. The sealed W3 configuration (hand_object_contact_weight=3, hinge=0, detach=false) remains the Phase 1B HOIPrior contact configuration.
next_action: Reshaping the attraction term's target is ruled out as a penetration fix. The evidence now points at the objective having an attractor and no repulsor, and at hand pose/orientation rather than palm-to-surface distance, as the remaining candidate explanations for the penetration deficit. User decides the next direction.

hypothesis: code/priors/hoi/losses.py builds every FK joint as root plus rotated rest-offset sums, so masked_hand_object_distance_loss has an undamped identity gradient path through prediction[...,0:3] while rotation gradients are moment-arm scaled; because its target is the model's own predicted object surface rather than GT palm position, translating the whole body is the cheapest self-referential descent direction, matching the monotone trans_dist dose-response degradation. Detaching root translation only inside this existing geometry term removes that path while leaving losses["fk"], velocity residuals and every other FK consumer attached, an objective-side intervention that cannot be absorbed as another generic model residual; full rationale and fixed rules are in docs/plan/PHASE_1B_HOI/06_GEOMETRY_TERM.md section 2026-08-14 Phase 1B P11.

hypothesis: The released InfBaGel code conjugated human_orient in both corpora and shipped rest_human_offsets_aligned.npy with the same conjugation baked in, and code/priors/core/window_codec.py took the window heading from pytorch3d's intrinsic ZXY[...,2] (the innermost, body-frame y) rather than the outermost world-y. On OMOMO the template conjugation cancels, so loss_fk was never geometrically wrong here (FK error 2.80e-07 m before vs 2.83e-07 m after; losses[fk] 1.10e-13 vs 1.07e-13) and the handover report's 0.56 m displacement is LINGO-only. What was defective on HOI is the window heading: the pre-fix canonicalisation removed 93.19 deg mean of a 42.21 deg mean true heading and roughly doubled the residual hip-azimuth spread relative to not canonicalising at all (p50 22.04 unshifted, 46.28 pre-fix, 2.13 post-fix), and the evaluator's step-0 window frame disagreed with the frame the model was trained on by 50.12 deg mean on 1 of 3 rollout windows while steps >=1 agreed exactly. P12 therefore repairs the representation frame across six files in one change and re-establishes the D2-AI baseline on the corrected representation. It claims a sampling-efficiency hypothesis plus evaluation consistency, NOT a repair of the cause of HOIPrior's ineffective iteration, which is measurement-refuted on OMOMO. Every D2-* model-side geometric row and the released baseline row are representation- and evaluator-invalidated and not recomputable, so no before/after difference may be reported across that boundary; the only controlled comparison is within this checkpoint, between a PRIMARY evaluation cell using the corrected step-0 frame and a CONTROL cell that reconstructs the historical step-0 rule by temporarily re-conjugating the corrected root and taking the scipy extrinsic yaw.

hypothesis: Hypothesis E: exposure bias / self-conditioning causes contraction because the model's own output is out of distribution, so GT history should restore each window toward window 1. Hypothesis M: the window mechanism contracts any absolute height, so GT history does not restore b and only stops compounding. Hypothesis F: dataset step-0 construction and window_codec.encode step >=1 construction differ and that difference itself causes contraction. Teacher forcing separates E from {M,F} but does not separate M from F; G4 separates the latter on CPU.

The frame-0 +2.75/+2.87 cm bias is not explained; window 1 is not teacher-forced, and a return of w2/w3 bias to frame-0 would only show a per-window constant, not its cause.

amended_interpretation_20260822.authorized_framing: A complete in-distribution ground-truth history recovers rho = 0.515/0.320 (cell G, windows 2/3) and 0.506/0.314 (cell N) of the gap to the ground-truth-conditioned window 1, i.e. +0.199 to +0.229 slope units with all four paired-bootstrap 95 percent CIs excluding zero. Compounding of a degraded history is therefore a real, measured contributor and rho is its size. The residual is the larger share: 0.485 of the window-2 gap and 0.680 of the window-3 gap survive a perfect history, and that residual per-window contraction is the main problem.
corroborating_facts_independent_of_the_E: window 1 already contracts from b = 1.025 at the first generated frame to b = 0.899 over its own 42 frames, from a ground-truth start with nothing accumulated
b_TF(w3) = 0.414 is far below b_TF(w2) = 0.708 although BOTH windows consumed a complete ground-truth history, so part of the depth dependence is not history quality at all
amended_interpretation_20260822.remedy_reading_is_a_bound_not_an_exclusi: Scheduled sampling or rollout fine-tuning may capture the rho fraction, but on this evidence their ceiling is the teacher-forced slope itself (b = 0.708/0.414 against b_ref = 0.899), so they cannot be the whole remedy and must not be the only next training direction. The earlier wording 'predicted NOT to fix the contraction' is replaced by this bound.
amended_interpretation_20260822.ruling: User ruling 2026-08-22: record P14 as teacher forcing PARTIALLY improving height tracking while the residual per-window height contraction remains the main problem. Do NOT record it as exposure bias being absent.
amended_interpretation_20260822.superseded_wording: The phrases 'intrinsic to the conditioning mechanism, not exposure bias', 'Exposure bias is ruled OUT as the dominant mechanism' and 'does NOT restore height-keeping ability ... leaves the per-window contraction untouched' overstate the result. lambda is a secondary discriminator; it bounds the exposure-bias mechanism's share and cannot establish that the mechanism is absent.
amended_interpretation_20260822.unchanged: No measured value in this record is altered and the PRIMARY classification stays tf-partial. Reframed reading surfaces: docs/HOIPRIOR_EVIDENCE_INDEX.md conclusion 23 and docs/phase_summaries/PHASE_1B_P14_ROLLOUT_TEACHER_FORCING.md.
amended_interpretation_20260822.what_lambda_establishes: lambda 0.018-0.045 establishes that the model's response slope is nearly the same whether the history level is ground truth or its own drifted output, so a clean history does not repair the per-window contraction. It does NOT establish that the exposure-bias mechanism contributes nothing; the measured rho is that contribution's size.

conclusion: A COMPLETE ground-truth history does NOT restore height-keeping ability. It removes the compounding (worth rho ~ 0.51 at window 2) and leaves the per-window contraction untouched: the model response slope to an in-distribution ground-truth history is indistinguishable from its response slope to its own degraded output (lambda 0.018-0.045).

hypothesis: Hypothesis E: exposure bias / self-conditioning causes contraction because the model's own output is out of distribution, so GT history should restore each window toward window 1. Hypothesis M: the window mechanism contracts any absolute height, so GT history does not restore b and only stops compounding. Hypothesis F: dataset step-0 construction and window_codec.encode step >=1 construction differ and that difference itself causes contraction. Teacher forcing separates E from {M,F} but does not separate M from F; G4 separates the latter on CPU.
manipulated_factor: For windows 2 and 3 only, history source changes from the model's previous-window output to dataset ground truth. Everything else is held fixed: checkpoint, 438 sequences, seed 42, noise, guidance setting, evaluation path, and default repaired step-0 frame rule.
next_action: Record that the per-window height contraction is intrinsic to the conditioning mechanism, not exposure bias, so the remedy class that treats it as exposure bias (scheduled sampling, rollout fine-tuning) is predicted to fail and should not be the next training run. The contraction is a property of how the model consumes an absolute-height history, which makes it load-bearing for the HOSI long-horizon chaining design: at b=0.19 by window 3, subject identity is already gone inside the released protocol own horizon. W3 geometry-term training stays on hold until the corrected P6 cell-U re-measurement lands.
non_claims: The teacher-forced arms 18 protocol metrics are NOT model scores and must never appear in /data/yujinlun/report/baseline.md, the evidence-index headline table, or any model comparison. They improve partly because windows 2 and 3 are anchored at the ground-truth location, which is construction, not capability.
The only authorized conclusion form is whether a COMPLETE ground-truth history restores height-keeping ability. It does not.

A recovery may NOT be attributed to the root-y channel alone: all five history channels were substituted. The vertical-only arm that could have isolated it was withdrawn after G4 showed it converts horizontal drift into object-translation error at full magnitude.
This does not reopen the D0 root-y repricing abort and provides no evidence for it.
Exposure bias is ruled OUT as the dominant mechanism, so scheduled sampling and rollout fine-tuning are predicted NOT to fix the contraction. That prediction is itself untested.
Only 3 windows were measured. Extrapolation to the many-window HOSI chain is an extrapolation, not a result.

G4 established that the 232-d conditioning tensor and its derived frame are equivalent between the step-0 and step-N paths. It did NOT cover obj_bps_data, object_goal_batch, pelvis_goal_batch or object_points_batch, so hypothesis F is excluded only for the channels G4 measured.
This says nothing about the frame-0 +2.75/+2.87 cm offset: window 1 is never teacher-forced.
This says nothing about the CHOIS-side deficit.

posthoc_conditional_bound_analysis_20260.authorized_framing: Under the conditional-mean assumption -- that squared-error training drives the model output toward E[y|x] -- the slope obtained by regressing that output on ground truth is constrained by the explainable-variance ceiling of the conditioning the predictor actually uses, so a slope below 1 is not by itself evidence of a defect. Measured against a history-only explainable-variance reference, window 2 under teacher forcing already sits close to that reference, and the large anomaly is concentrated in window 3 and in the normal rollout.
posthoc_conditional_bound_analysis_20260.consequence_that_changes_no_classificati: This record normalizes rho by b_ref = b(w1) = 0.899, while the history-only reference differs across the spans being compared (0.5889 at w1 against 0.7537 at w2 and 0.7154 at w3), so that denominator is not an equal-information yardstick across spans. rho, the confidence intervals and tf-partial are unchanged. What this adds is that at window 2 the residual per-window contraction is smaller relative to what that span's history can explain than the raw gap to 0.899 suggests, and that the deficit is concentrated in window 3 and in the normal rollout.

not_authorized_readings: That the tracking slope IS the R^2 of the conditioning. That must not be written unconditionally: it holds only under the conditional-mean assumption, and window 1 contradicts it at 1.53x the history-only reference.
That the history-only reference is an upper bound on this model. It is not; the model has conditioning beyond the history.

That tf-partial, the PRIMARY readout, or the amended_interpretation_20260822 framing changes. Teacher forcing partially improves height tracking and the residual per-window contraction remains the main problem; that reading stands.
That window 2 is therefore solved. The teacher-forced arm is non-deployable by construction: it consumed a ground-truth history that does not exist at inference.

posthoc_conditional_bound_analysis_20260.status: POST-HOC MECHANISM ANALYSIS, appended 2026-08-22 on user ruling. It is NOT part of the preregistration, NOT a gate, and NOT a re-measurement of this experiment. posthoc_conditional_bound_analysis_20260.why_this_is_an_assumption_and_not_an_ide: The model is not verified to be a conditional-mean predictor, and one measured value shows the history-only reference is NOT a hard ceiling on it: at window 1 the normal-arm slope is 0.9017 against a history-only reference of 0.5889, i.e. 1.53x the reference. The model conditions on text_embedding, object_bps, goals and progress in addition to the 2-frame history, so its attainable slope is not capped by a history-only figure. This record therefore does NOT assert that the tracking slope IS the R^2 of the conditioning. It asserts only the bounded comparison in authorized_framing, under the stated assumption.

hypothesis: The hand-object geometry term, with its per-hand contact mask defect repaired and its weight set to the output-space gradient-norm-equalized dose w_geom* = 0.016016425, changes HOIPrior's contact behaviour relative to the identical recipe with the term absent. Under the sealed D2-AI recipe at 299,520,000 windows on the corrected representation frame, the control is P12 (p1-hoi-p12-frame-repair-baseline-s42-20260819), which ran the term OFF. The prior evidence is that eleven model-side interventions did not move contact engagement and that the geometry lineage (P8/P9/P9c dose sweep, P10 formula repair, P11 root detach) closed negative; this arm tests whether a REPAIRED reducer at a PRINCIPLED dose behaves differently from that closed lineage, whose doses were all chosen on the defective reducer by loss-magnitude matching.
interpretation_boundaries: 1. TREATMENT PACKAGE, NOT A MASK ABLATION. This arm tests 'the corrected geometry term enabled as a package'. Because a zero weight makes the mask mode inert (losses.py:379), P15-versus-P12 cannot attribute any outcome to the mask reducer alone, nor to the dose alone. Isolating the reducer would require a third arm at the same dose with hand_object_contact_mask_mode=sealed, which this preregistration does NOT authorize.

2. EXPLORATORY EQUALIZATION DOSE, NOT NINE-DIGIT PRECISION. 0.016016425 is a gradient-norm equalization dose accepted after a G7 human review, and it is an ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE estimate. RC1, the batch-size invariance check, returned 0.6141 for per_hand_per_frame (and 0.4675 for sealed) rather than ~1.0, and remains confounded with batch COUNT (8 vs 16), so the derivation is not shown to be invariant to the measurement batch. The digits are recorded for exact reproducibility of THIS arm, not as a claim of precision. Additional caveats that bound the number: the human/object side ratio is 0.2506 and intrinsically unbalanceable by one scalar (G7), shard 0's geometry gradient is 1.60x the other shards and pulls the 20-cell geomean down, and the weight was derived at ONE checkpoint.

3. W3's weight=3 IS NOT PORTABLE AND IS NOT A COMPARISON POINT FOR THIS DOSE. W3 (hand_object_contact_weight=3.0) came from the P8/P9/P9c eight-point empirical sweep that walked the weight from 50 down to 3 by matching the geometry term's LOSS MAGNITUDE against object_surface (8.47 vs 9.02). P15's weight is set by a different criterion in a different space: equalizing the geometry term's GRADIENT NORM against the geometric mean of the non-geometry side norms. The two numbers therefore have different dimensions and different purposes, and the ~3000x gap between 50 and 0.016 is the criterion change, not a contradiction or a correction. Additionally, every P8-P11 dose was measured on the DEFECTIVE reducer, in which the free (non-contacting) hand contributed 97.13% of the geometry floor; the repaired reducer drops that floor by 27x, so the old sweep's doses do not transfer even within their own criterion.

4. A NULL NEGATES THE DOSE, NOT THE DIRECTION. If this arm is null, the conclusion is bounded to 'the geometry term at THIS dose, with THIS reducer, at THIS budget, on THIS checkpoint's derivation, did not move the preregistered metrics'. It does NOT close the geometry-term direction, does not establish that no dose works, and does not retroactively validate or invalidate the P10/P11 negative closures. One dose is one point on a dose-response curve that this arm does not measure.

stop_rules_all_mechanical: R1 NON-FINITE: any of total, reconstruction, fk, object_surface, hand_object_contact_geometry is NaN or Inf, or the logged `finite` flag is not true -> STOP.
R2 MISSING TERM: the first validation entry does not contain the key hand_object_contact_geometry -> STOP (the configured objective was not the executed objective).

R3 LEVEL: total_p12_equivalent > 1.25 * 0.12664846108100392 = 0.15831057635125490 -> STOP. Derived from P12's own trajectory: its first point is the global maximum of the whole run and the largest point-to-point rise anywhere in 97 steps is 1.0380x, so 1.25x leaves 1.20x headroom over the largest movement the control ever exhibited.
R4 GEOMETRY TERM DEGENERATE: hand_object_contact_geometry is exactly 0.0 at the first validation point -> STOP (the mask engaged nothing, so the treatment was not applied).
R5 PROCESS: the trainer exits non-zero, a rank dies, or no first validation point is written by 1.5x the control's time to that point -> STOP.

hypothesis: Phase 1C entry amendment, preregistered before any source change. Measured finding: the released LINGO dataset mislabels its mirrored half. Sequences 9725..19449 are exact x-mirrors of 0..9724 (transl_aligned x bitwise negated, y/z bitwise equal, lengths equal for all 9,725 pairs) yet every frame of that half is labelled '005_mirror' although the underlying rooms are 110 distinct scenes; the correct <src>_mirror occupancy grids all exist on disk and satisfy grid(<src>_mirror) == grid(<src>)[::-1] bitwise, but 143 of 254 grids are never referenced. LINGO's own loader inherits this (lingo/code/datasets/lingo.py:186). Two consequences: (i) any model keyed on the label conditions ~1.12M of 2.28M windows on the wrong room's geometry; (ii) experiments/splits/lingo_scene_disjoint_seed42.json is family-disjoint by label but content-duplicated, with 1,895 of 1,895 validation sequences having their exact x-mirror on the train side (234,381 frames), so it cannot measure generalization. ReMoGen, the only published LINGO split, was evaluated and rejected: its split is random per-segment (README:252; the '# === Scene-based split assignment ===' comment at extract_dataset_lingo_hsi.py:372 sits above code that never implements it), holding out 0 of 75 families with 87 of 88 test scenes also in train, 70.3% of test segments having their x-mirror twin in train, 98.3% of test captions appearing verbatim in train, 46.6% of its advertised test set silently dropped by dataset_lingo.py:59-60, no human-scene penetration metric at all, and zero published LINGO table rows to be comparable to. This amendment therefore replaces scene-family-disjoint-v1 with an additive v2 that relabels mirrors from verified structure and produces a three-way family-disjoint split, and preregisters the native-domain geometry evaluator. The Phase 1C baseline is fixed to the released InfBaGel checkpoint alone (user decision); since it trained on 45 LINGO scenes selected deterministically by all_scenes[:45] (config_train_infbagel_mix.yaml:15, datasets/infbagel_mix.py:322) and 005_mirror is not among them, the v2 test set is drawn from the 32 scene families that selection never touched, making baseline and HSIPrior both zero-shot on test.

hypothesis: Same-day correction to the evaluator geometry source, made before any model measurement exists. The earlier row designated Scene/<scene>.npy boolean occupancy as the primary geometry for penetration, with mesh_low.obj as a cross-check. That is backwards. Measured: scene 004 occupancy fraction is 0.5119, and occupancy by height slice is NOT concentrated at furniture height - the y~1.98 m ceiling slice is the MOST occupied at 0.807, which is impossible for solid geometry. LINGO's own dataset documentation reads '1' as 'occupied by scene objects OR unreachable', so the array is a reachability/free-space volume, not geometry. Consequences measured on GT motion: GT joints fall in 'occupied' voxels 7.1% of the time in aggregate (1.37%-8.95% by scene) and 4.3% of GT joints lie outside the world bbox entirely, so an occupancy-based penetration metric has a GT reference near 0.07 rather than 0 and a model that hovers away from every surface scores BETTER than ground truth - design prior #7's exact failure mode, here as a property of the metric rather than of a model. Correction: mesh_low.obj becomes the primary geometry for all penetration and contact scoring; the occupancy grid remains the model's conditioning input and is reported only as an explicitly labelled 'reachability violation' diagnostic, never as penetration. Feasibility verified: all 110 non-mirrored referenced scenes have a mesh (0 missing), 004/mesh_low.obj is watertight with 1,012,799 vertices and 2,025,986 faces, its bbox nests inside the grid bbox with floor at y~0. Scene_mesh contains no _mirror meshes, which is sufficient because split v2 draws validation and test from non-mirrored sequences only. This row also pins the exact metric formulas, because a literature survey found that Pene_mean/Pene_max are at least four mutually incompatible quantities sharing one symbol: the same LINGO baseline is reported at 0.402, 0.421, 0.392 and 1397 across four papers. Citing 'following DIMOS/LINGO' is therefore not a definition, and every reported quantity must carry its expression, aggregation order, unit and sign convention.

hypothesis: Correction of a factual error in the Phase 1C entry, raised by the user and confirmed against the author's own documentation. The superseded row asserted that the released InfBaGel checkpoint was trained by config_train_infbagel_mix.yaml with lingo_scene_num 45, i.e. on OMOMO plus 45 LINGO scenes. That was inferred from the presence of the mix config in the repository rather than from evidence about the artifact, and it is wrong. readme.md:81 states the released checkpoint is a consistency model 'trained on OMOMO dataset only', and readme.md:133 presents mix as an optional variant whose weights were never released. Two independent facts agree: the checkpoint contains embedding_hand_goal.* and no embedding_scene_goal.*, and commit 262f2d9 named that module GoalEncoder(mode='hand') while 75efccc renamed it to mode='scene', so the weights predate this repository's rename and are the author's original artifact; and the author's own sampling defaults are dataset omomo_test, model infbagel with is_mix false, sample_type consistency. Consequence: the released checkpoint never saw LINGO, so it is zero-shot on all 110 LINGO scenes and all 76 families, and the v2 rule that reserved the test side as the families the baseline had not touched bought nothing. It did cost training data, which matters now that the Phase 1C plan trains the diffusion and consistency baselines on LINGO only: v2 allocated just 976,993 of 1,939,898 eligible windows to train, 50.4%, and discarded 481,535 held-out-family mirror windows. Hence scene-family-disjoint-v3, an additive third algorithm that drops the baseline rule and partitions all 76 families by eligible source window count at 0.70/0.10/0.20, with the mirror repair, the mirror discard rule and every other v2 invariant unchanged. Ratios are defined over the source (non-mirror) pool because mirrors are train-side augmentation; targeting a mirror-inclusive pool while accumulating source-only counts for held-out sides mixes units and starved validation to 4 families in the first attempt. Families are assigned largest-source-window-first to the side with the largest deficit, with seed 42 breaking ties. Two scene-count floors are enforced because results are reported per scene and scene variance dominates the metrics: test at least 25 scenes, validation at least 12.

conclusion: Completed with TRAINER_EXIT=0 in 10 h 25 m 01 s (10.4169 h, 41.7 GPU-h), a 0.94% overrun on the preregistered 10.32 h, so the OMP-capped budget held. All 58,678 of 58,678 preregistered optimizer updates ran; the cap landed mid-epoch-89 (step 294 of 656) as preregistered. Zero non-finite gradient norms across 4 ranks x 58,678 updates and zero Traceback/RuntimeError/OOM/nan in the log. One isolated post-warmup gradient excursion, 0.830289 at update 28403 (epoch 43, step 195), neighbours 0.037/0.034; loss rose from the epoch 40-42 step-190 band (~0.001710) to a peak 0.001908 at step 220 (+11.6%) and returned inside the epoch 40-42 step-300 band by step 280. Gradient clipping stayed off and this run supplies the evidence it was right: max_norm=1.0 would clip 0 post-warmup updates and would not have caught the excursion either, since the second-largest post-warmup norm is 0.7736 - the excursion is the top of a continuous tail, not a separable outlier. Gate artefact epoch089.pth (sha256 8527b03ae9003c884b0af94fce26f9e9a063f301c39cdfcacb18962a0e20a0d6) loads strict with 218 keys, 0 missing, 0 unexpected, and is genuinely distilled rather than a teacher copy: the whole 116-tensor frozen set is bitwise unchanged while 100 of 102 trainable tensors moved (relative L2 change min 0.020, median 0.410, max 0.868). The 2 trainable tensors that did not move are embedding_output.weight/bias, a module built at code/models/infbagel.py:1162 and never used in forward, so it takes no gradient - 0.30% of parameter elements, pre-existing in the author's architecture. Training loss plateaued in an epoch-end band of 0.001641-0.001874 from epoch 30 on; recorded as observation only, since this project has measured that held-out loss anticorrelates with native rollout metrics.

The cross-checkout 2.30 CM/diffusion multiplier and the 26.7 h / 107 GPU-h it implied are DISCARDED, not approved; this branch has its own measurement and nothing may be re-derived from 2.30. The branch own CM/diffusion ratio is 1.57-1.60.

omp_cap_neutrality=the OMP cap is a scheduling change, not a numerical one. 8 direct capped-vs-uncapped pairs (O1,O2,X1,X2 x B1,B2) are bitwise identical, each on 300 distinct post-allreduce global gradient norms (logged 4x, once per rank) and 120 stdout losses. Positive control: fresh uncapped reps reproduce the archived ones bitwise across sessions. Negative control: raising world size from 4 to 8 and changing nothing else makes 1200/1200 records differ, 4.6012 pct at update 1 and median 18.46 pct across the window. Sensitivity: one ULP of the logged float64 norms is 1.11e-16 to 2.22e-16 relative, and the capped pairs differ in no digit. Mechanism observed live: 1344 OS threads across 12 processes on 112 hardware threads uncapped, 176 at cap 4.

layout_rejection=the 8x256 layout is rejected on process-neutrality, NOT on speed. code/models/infbagel.py:1257-1259 overwrites cfg_scale to -1 for the entire rank-local batch keyed on the timestep of sample 0 alone; consistency_loss draws start_timestep from 25 discretized values whose maximum is 499, so it fires with p=1/25 per rank per step, and :1320-1325 then zeroes every temporal scene embedding for every sample in that batch. Combined with per-rank seeding seed+rank at code/train_infbagel.py:326-329, 8 ranks and 4 ranks compute different things on provably identical data (4.6012 pct divergence in the update-1 gradient norm). The expected zeroed fraction is the same 4 pct in both layouts; only the realized trajectory differs. The measured 2.02x per-update speed gap was taken uncapped, where the 8-rank layout runs 24 processes instead of 12 against the same 112 threads, so it is confounded by exactly the pathology the cap removes and cannot carry the verdict. The defect is inherited from run B and from the author code and is DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED so that C stays comparable to its own teacher.

gradient_clipping=none. Deferred by the user pending the post-warmup distribution at update 2000. The 300-update probe (min 0.0219, median 0.0602, max 0.1910, zero non-finite) lies entirely inside the 2000-update warmup at no more than 15.0 pct of the target learning rate, and its trend is window-dependent, swinging from -32.1 pct to +74.2 pct, so it supplies no defensible max_norm. This run launches unclipped with +log_grad_norm=true precisely so the threshold can be chosen from measured post-warmup data.

is_mix_resolved=model.infbagel.is_mix=false AND sampler.pelvis.is_mix=false, read from the resolved config rather than inferred from defaults. Run B needed a dedicated commit e99d3f2 because setting one side only is silently wrong.

resolved_config_preflight=results/hsi_c_lingo_cm/preflight/config_resolved_preflight.yaml, generated at the launch commit with the exact overrides, unresolved interpolations 0, sha256 76ddff311dfdcd5e99582c7e001c19a8b4d2628075e368442420925d4e427aaa. AGENTS.md:189-191; run B shipped without this and C closes the gap.

instrument_bitwise_inert_when_off=re-verified on this branch today: two 12-update arms of this exact config, one without the flag at all, produce epoch000.pth with identical sha256 b552009d66129a8058e19a5185c1f80da069c57bee5632141acfbca03c035bad (179662353 bytes, 218 tensors, 50.01M elements) and identical last_loss 0.0029015124309808016; grad_norms/ appears only in the enabled arm. Enabling it costs +3584 bytes of per-rank peak allocated and does not move the numbers.
authority_suite=200 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 3 skipped, run on the exact tree that was committed, before this manifest

hardware_assignment_reading=hardware_assignment records the pool each expert owns; HSI owns the 8-GPU authority host and this run allocates 4 of those cards. experiments/training_resource_protocol.json is deliberately unamended.

provenance_note=provenance is recorded at metrics-write time, so no commit may be created while this run is in flight; both preregistration commits precede the launch deliberately

Guided minus unguided per-window wall clock over guidance applications per window (499 at 500 diffusion steps, ~15 at 16 consistency steps) gives 0.0832 s/application for B and 0.1090 s for C -- slightly MORE expensive after distillation -- making guidance 72% of B's guided cost and 83.2% of C's. Full 26-scene coverage in a latency subset is arithmetically impossible at any 45-60 min budget: 8 scenes have a minimum episode of 33-50 windows and the per-scene minima sum to 394 windows, about 6.65 h guided; all *-new_loco scenes plus 071-write, 082-wash-brush_teeth, 086-pick_up-put_down and 097-drum_kit are structurally excluded, which costs scene diversity in the penetration branch rather than any horizon effect.

# Layout: 4 GPUs x micro-batch 512 x accum 1. Measured 0.71223 s/update against

# the arms are disjoint by 28x the widest within-arm spread). See registry
# amendment p1-hsi-b-layout-4x512-s42-20260814. Fallback is 8 x 256 x accum 1,

# 2026-08-19: both of those numbers were measured with OMP_NUM_THREADS unset, and
# so was run p1-hsi-b-lingo-full-s42-20260814 itself -- its launch.sh carries only
# CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, which is why it sustained 0.7305 s/update. Re-measured
# with the same three-interleaved-reps protocol, both layouts, capped and
# uncapped:
#     8 x 256 capped 0.38674   uncapped 0.92446
#     4 x 512 capped 0.52189   uncapped 0.71844
# The uncapped pair reproduces the registered pair, so the amendment was measured
# in a regime that does not apply to a capped host, and the ranking reverses
# under the cap. THIS LAYOUT IS UNCHANGED ANYWAY: 8 x 256 is faster (15.71 h vs
# 21.20 h projected over 146,255 updates) but changing rank count is not
# optimization-neutral here -- the two layouts differ by 4.60% in global gradient
# norm at update 1 while the trainer is bitwise deterministic within a layout,
# caused by models/infbagel.py:1257 overwriting cfg_scale for the whole rank-local
# batch from sample 0's timestep, plus per-rank seeding seed+rank. Speed does not
# license that change; 5.5 h does not either.
#

# this layout (29.6 h -> 21.2 h). Unset, 8 ranks spawn 2671 OS threads on 112
# cores and 4 ranks spawn 1334.

# loss_w_obj_pts is inert on this branch: under lingo_only every sample takes the
# no-object branch, so mask_points is empty, loss_object is None at every update
# (measured over 4000), and this weight multiplies nothing.
loss_w_obj_pts: 50
# Was 50, the released value.  Lowered after a matched A/B at 50 vs 3 over 4000
# updates (identical seed and data order, bit-identical at update 1 on all 8
# ranks).  50 puts loss_fk at 94.6% of the gradient norm even at update 4000 and
# on ~90% of coordinates, in a direction essentially orthogonal to the rest of
# the objective: cos(g_jrot, g_fk) is +0.067 against a 0.00116 random baseline in
# that 473,088-dim space, so 0.45% of FK's rotation-channel push is aligned and
# 45.9x of it is not.  loss_jrot cannot resist -- it is L1, so |g_jrot| is
# exactly constant at 1/sqrt(473088) no matter how far the channel has stalled.
#
# The consequence is not subtle.  At 50 the predicted root attitude degrades
# monotonically, 85.8 deg off world +y at update 250 to 122.48 deg at 4000
# (cross-rank [121.30, 123.61]); at 3 it snaps to 9.4 deg by update 750 and holds
# 7.13 deg, against ground truth 7.83.  122.48 deg is within 0.2 deg of the
# 122.68 deg snap recorded for the previous trained checkpoint -- so with all
# three representation defects fixed, this weight alone still reproduces the
# failure the whole repair was about.
#
# Why the term cannot see it: loss_fk scores 4 hand and 4 foot joints only, and
# the kinematic chain can satisfy those from any root attitude by compensating
# upstream.  Measured -- at update 4000 both arms have the same end-effector
# error (0.2130 m hand / 0.1690 m foot at 50 vs 0.2126 / 0.1714 at 3) and the
# same loss_fk (within 1%), while their root attitudes differ by 115 deg.  Paying
# 50x buys nothing on its own term and costs the rotation channel.
#
# 3 is the gradient-parity weight measured at update 4000.  The naive parity
# figure of 2.86 against the whole base objective is contaminated and was not
# used: |g_object| is 99.5% of |g_base| there and grows 16x while its output-space
# norm stays flat, because under lingo_only channels 216:232 carry an exactly
# constant target and two L1 terms keep a non-decaying gradient against it.  The
# meaningful parity weights are 1.09 against loss_jrot on 84:216 and 0.33 against
# jpos+jrot; aligned-signal break-even is 16.1.  At 3, all five base terms, both
# attitude metrics and the 6-D column norm are better than at 50 and loss_fk is
# tied -- 50 wins nothing recorded.
#
# Caveats: 4000 updates is 2.7% of this run's 146,255 and sits inside the 2,000
# update warmup, so this fixes direction and magnitude, not the converged value.
# FK pressure may matter more once the coarse pose is right, a regime neither arm
# reached; if end-effector precision disappoints at full budget, 16.1 is the next
# value and that is a new experiment, not a tweak.  C's loss_w_fk of 1 needs no
# change: consistency_loss has no loss_jrot to be starved, and 1 already sits
# below B's 1.09 rotation-channel parity.
loss_w_fk: 3

gradient_anomaly_scan.comparison_to_20260814: The prior run recorded two entries, ratio 5.94 at epoch 10 step 50 and ratio 3.66 at epoch 160 step 340, the latter an isolated mid-training event that cost roughly 23 epochs of progress. This run has no analogue: the largest excursion anywhere in 223 epochs is 1.09, which is ordinary minibatch variance.
gradient_anomaly_scan.method: All 14,492 logged (epoch, step) points, each the mean of the four ranks' printed losses, scanned for point-to-point ratio; the same quantity the 20260814 record's two entries were flagged on.

results.gradient_clipping: none -- code/train_infbagel.py applies no clipping; unchanged for this run, but now for a measured reason rather than for want of a measurement. B's own post-warmup global norm distribution has min 1.0394 and median 5.9947, so max_norm=1.0 would have clipped all 144,255 post-warmup updates (and 146,253 of all 146,255; only 2 updates in the whole run, both inside warmup, ever fell at or below 1.0) -- it would be a global LR rescale, not an outlier guard. Compare run C's 2026-08-16 distribution: min 0.0130, median 0.0543, max 0.8303. B's median is 110x C's, and C's entire range sits below the threshold that would clip every B update. That is direct evidence C's distribution was never a valid substitute for B's, and that the earlier refusal to pick a B threshold from C's numbers was correct. A grounded B threshold would now be derivable from this distribution, but it is not needed for this run: with max/median 4.37 and no isolated spike there is no outlier for clipping to catch.

gradient_norm_distribution_post_warmup.interpretation: The heavy tail is a single cluster at the warmup boundary, where the LR schedule has just reached 0.0002 -- all five largest norms fall in updates 2017-2167, within 167 updates of the boundary. There is no isolated late spike, and the largest norm in the whole run is only 4.37x the median. This is a different phenomenon from the 20260814 run's epoch-160 event, which was an isolated excursion in steady state.
gradient_norm_distribution_post_warmup.source: results/hsi_b_lingo_full_v2/grad_norms/grad_norms_rank0.jsonl, produced by +log_grad_norm=true; the global DDP norm is rank-invariant after all-reduce, so rank 0 is the whole distribution.

results.metrics_note: Training workload only. No rollout/native-domain metric is claimed by this record; the run-B evaluation is a separate workload with its own registry row. final_train_loss_epoch222_mean is NOT comparable to the 20260814 run's 0.20213253051042557: the objective's composition changed between the two runs (loss_w_fk 50 -> 3, applied to an FK term that was itself wrong before the representation fix), so the two scalars are sums over differently weighted, differently computed terms and their ratio carries no information about model quality. Both are computed on the same basis -- the mean of all 248 logged epoch-222 loss values across the four ranks. The 20260814 record's key train_loss_epoch158_mean_pre_spike is deliberately absent here rather than set to null: it named the pre-spike reference level for that run's isolated epoch-160 loss excursion, and this run has no spike to reference (see gradient_anomaly_scan). Two launch differences from 20260814 are recorded above and are both deliberate: OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, bitwise identical and worth 1.38x (29.67 h -> 20.98 h), and +log_grad_norm=true, which produced gradient_norm_distribution_post_warmup.

objective_weights.loss_w_fk_note: Lowered 50 -> 3 for this run on the basis of the 4000-update matched A/B recorded in code/config/config_train_hsi_b_lingo_full.yaml. At 50 the predicted root attitude degraded monotonically to 122.48 deg off world +y while loss_fk itself was unchanged; 3 is the measured gradient-parity weight at update 4000.
objective_weights.loss_w_obj_pts_inert_reason: Under lingo_only every sample takes the no-object branch, so mask_points is empty and loss_object is None at every update; this weight multiplies nothing in this run. The value is carried unchanged from the released config and is recorded for provenance, not because it had an effect.

conclusion: Training completed cleanly. TRAINER_EXIT=0 at 2026-08-20T10:10:23+08:00, 90 epochs entered, 58,678 of 58,678 optimizer updates logged, 10.3858 h wall clock, 0.63719 s/update. That is like-for-like with the 20260816 run's 0.6391 s/update and 10.4169 h -- both ran with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 -- and 0.3% faster, unlike the B v2 versus B comparison where the older run had no OMP cap at all. As by construction and identically to the 20260816 run, the update budget closes mid-epoch at epoch 89 step 294 of 656 (58,678 / 656 = 89.45), so epoch089.pth is the weights at update 58,678 written by the epoch == cfg.epochs - 1 branch of code/train_infbagel.py:580-582 rather than by ckpt_interval. Six epoch checkpoints plus one resume checkpoint are sha256-bound in results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2/metrics.json; the gate artefact epoch089.pth hashes to f1c09c2425af3d45936da80590e98647d616f777fe4059f1067e6140c72f852e. The teacher is bound to B v2's epoch222 at 5daaf813ca82878868602840760f35df43b642d73f73cb37e24bb5a4dbf62b4c, matching p1-hsi-b-lingo-full-v2-s42-20260819 independently. Numerical health: zero non-finite gradient norms in 58,678 updates, all four ranks bitwise equal at every update, and no isolated gradient excursion of the kind the 20260816 run recorded (norm 0.830289 at update 28403) -- the largest point-to-point ratio in the four-rank mean logged loss across 5,814 logged points is 1.628 and falls at an epoch boundary, where step 20 is compared against the previous epoch's step 650. Post-warmup DDP global gradient norm over 56,678 updates: min 0.0058, median 0.0799, mean 0.1003, max 0.8995. That median sits in the same regime as the 20260816 run's 0.0543 and roughly 75x BELOW run B v2's 5.9947, measured on the identical host and layout, which establishes the B-versus-C gradient-scale gap as a property of the diffusion versus consistency objective rather than of any defect. max_norm=1.0 clips 0 post-warmup updates here while clipping all 144,255 of B v2's, so a single threshold cannot serve both stages and clipping stays off. Final train loss is NOT comparable to the 20260816 run's: the teacher differs and that teacher was itself trained under a different objective. NO scientific or geometric metric is claimed by this row -- the health checks and the C+guided evaluation are separate records and were not complete when this row was written.

hypothesis: Phase 1C model C: consistency-model distillation of run B v2, retrained after the four defect repairs of 2026-08-18/19 (3ded4eb rotation and joint channels in worlds 90 deg apart, so loss_fk scored against a skeleton displaced 0.5578 m mean; a4c979c the joint channel normalized with OMOMO's norm.npy and denormalized with LINGO's, up to 1.0263 m round-trip and a mis-centred scene-occupancy query; bcb4ad4 mask_fk computed but never applied in p_losses; eb5bc1b loss_w_fk 50 -> 3, where 50 alone drove predicted root attitude to 122.48 deg in a matched 4000-update A/B). Budget, layout, data and seed are identical to p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-s42-20260816 -- LINGO-only v3 train partition, effective batch 2048 (4 GPUs x 512 x accum 1), 58,678 optimizer updates / 90 epochs, seed 42, bf16+TF32, w=1, cm_timesteps 16 -- so the two C runs differ only in the repaired representation and in their teacher. loss_w_fk stays 1 here deliberately while B's moved to 3: consistency_loss is a single term over all 232 channels against the EMA teacher, so there is no loss_jrot to starve, and 1 already sits below B v2's measured 1.09 rotation-channel gradient parity. Output goes to results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2/ because the 20260816 artifacts back a registered row and AGENTS.md:126-127 forbids overwriting them. This row seals the TRAINING workload only. Under the user's 2026-08-18 protocol this checkpoint is the ONLY one this branch evaluates, and only in the guided cell.
next_action: Read the four health checks of section 7 of /data/yujinlun/report/ 蔚金伦_260818 handover report on hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2_epoch089.pth BEFORE spending evaluation budget. The most sensitive is the within-window root-rotation increment at coarse step 1->2 (history_frames=2, so frame 1 is the last real history frame): ground truth 9.62 deg, healthy per-step 1.7-4.2 deg, the pre-fix checkpoint 122.68 deg. The other three are pelvis up-axis off vertical (GT 10.10 deg versus 90.58 broken), joint-channel bone-length CV (control 2.4e-7 versus 0.101 broken), and FK pelvis-to-neck off +y (GT 8.59 deg versus 95.15 broken); all four are conjugation-invariant or independently anchored, so anchor each by running the same code path on ground truth first. Then evaluate C+guided only, against results/lingo_hsi/ground-truth-v3, which survives all four fixes bitwise because GroundTruthSource reads DATASET_ROOT directly. Assert positively that the guidance path executed: 087848f once silently broke every guided cell including the gate and a hasattr guard hid it. Do not share a table with any pre-fix model row -- schema_version separates them, and every pre-fix model-side geometric number is representation-invalidated and not recomputable. The Phase 1C gate threshold itself remains deferred by the user and is not defined here.

results.budget_note: The preregistered budget is 58,678 optimizer updates = 89.45 epochs at 656 steps/epoch, so max_optimizer_updates stops mid-epoch at epoch 89 step 294 of 656. epoch089.pth is therefore the weights at update 58,678 and is written by the epoch == cfg.epochs - 1 branch (code/train_infbagel.py:580-582), not the ckpt_interval branch. Same off-by-a-partial-epoch as the 20260816 C run, by construction.

gate_artefact.selection_rule: final weights at the preregistered update budget (58,678), not a best-of selection

gradient_anomaly_scan.basis: mean over ranks at each logged (epoch, step); max adjacent ratio
gradient_anomaly_scan.note: No isolated gradient excursion of the kind the 20260816 C run recorded (norm 0.830289 at update 28403). The largest loss step-ratio here is 1.628 and falls at an epoch boundary, where step 20 is compared against the previous epoch's step 650.

results.gradient_clipping: none - code/train_infbagel.py applies no clipping. Retained deliberately: max_norm=1.0 clips 0 of 56678 post-warmup updates here, while the same threshold would have clipped all 144,255 of run B v2's. A single threshold cannot serve both stages.

That establishes the B-vs-C gradient-scale gap as a property of the diffusion vs consistency objective, not of any defect, and it is why C's distribution was never a valid substitute for B's when choosing a clipping threshold.

results.metrics_note: Training workload only. No rollout, native-domain, or gate metric is claimed by this record. The final train loss is NOT comparable to the 20260816 C run: the teacher differs, and that teacher was itself trained under a different objective (loss_w_fk 3 on a corrected FK term versus 50 on a term carrying a 0.5614 m^2 irreducible floor). Health checks on this checkpoint and the C+guided evaluation are separate records.
results.objective: consistency-model distillation from run B v2 (sample_type=consistency)

objective_weights.loss_w_fk_note: Deliberately unchanged while B v2 went 50 -> 3. consistency_loss (models/infbagel.py:363-370) is a single term over all 232 channels against the EMA teacher, so there is no loss_jrot to be starved, and 1 already sits below B v2's measured 1.09 rotation-channel gradient parity. See the 2026-08-19 plan-doc section.
objective_weights.loss_w_obj_pts_note: Inert under lingo_only: loss_object is None at every update because mask_points is ANDed with is_object.

teacher.note: Post-representation-fix teacher. Distilling from the pre-fix hsi_b_lingo_full epoch222 would have faithfully preserved its 122 deg rotation channel.

conclusion: 375/375, schema_version 4, finite_motion 375/375, 1 h 0 m 01 s wall clock, 375 motion NPZ exported. FOUNDATION FIRST: recomputing ground truth on the fixed tree is BITWISE identical to the sealed ground-truth-v3 row across all 375 sequences and all 50 numeric keys, differing only in schema_version (2 vs 4). The earlier claim rested on 20 episodes; it now rests on the full set, so every v4-versus-GT comparison below is valid despite the schema gap. 10,000x paired bootstrap, seed 42, strata caption=='walk' (130) versus interactive (245). ALL 375: five metrics are now statistically INDISTINGUISHABLE from ground truth — pene_pct_scene 0.98x (ns), contact_count 1.03x (ns), fs_nemf 1.00x (ns), fs_nemf_ankle 0.99x (ns), fs_nemf_toe 1.00x (ns), plus success_min_10cm 0.99x (ns) — and four are significantly BETTER than ground truth: pen_ratio 0.77x, interior_jerk 0.89x, skate_ratio 0.79x, transition_distance_aligned 0.84x. Significantly worse: boundary_jerk 1.60x (+50.4 [38.7, 63.7]), jerk_ratio 1.70x, pene_sum_mean_floorexcl 1.37x, pen_depth_max 1.23x, goal_height_err_m 1.12x, pen_depth_mean 1.03x, success_last_10cm 0.9733; and against a GT of exactly zero, goal_planar_err_m 0.0471 m, last_dist 0.0253 m, min_dist 0.0044 m. Compare the pre-fix c_guided_v3 row, where EVERY metric except foot skate was significantly worse than GT: pen_ratio 2.40x, contact_count 2.14x, boundary_jerk 80.90x, success_last_10cm 0.4133, goal_planar_err 0.3390 m. THREE FINDINGS THAT OVERTURN PRIOR CONCLUSIONS. (1) boundary_jerk was recorded as the largest GT gap and as surviving both distillation and guidance (guidance moved it 0.7%, rank correlation 0.9996). It did NOT survive the representation repair: 6831 -> 134.9, a ~50x improvement. This is same-instrument: git log confirms 3ded4eb touched only penetration_metrics, fs_nemf and skate_ratio in code/priors/hsi/metrics.py and left every jerk function untouched. The internal control agrees — transition_distance_aligned, which is invariant to global rotation, is 0.84x GT (significantly BETTER), so seam POSITION continuity now beats ground truth while third-derivative smoothness at the seam remains 1.60x. The residual is high-frequency seam jitter, not a positional jump. (2) The pre-fix fs_nemf of 0.33x GT was vacuous: 208 of 375 sequences scored exactly 0 because the FK body lay flat and the feet never entered the ankle/toe bands. Post-fix only 5 score 0 (GT: 0) and the value is 1.00x GT — the metric went from flattering-because-broken to real-and-at-parity. (3) The 59% goal shortfall was mostly an evaluator decoding defect, not model undershoot: goal_planar_err_m 0.3390 -> 0.0471 m, last_dist 0.1435 -> 0.0253 m, success_last_10cm 0.4133 -> 0.9733. This is the first measurement that separates the two, and the ~0.4x horizontal compression explains most of it. STRATIFICATION IS THE ACTIONABLE RESULT, and the all-375 mean hides it. On walk 130 the model matches or beats ground truth almost everywhere: success_last_10cm and success_min_10cm both exactly 1.0000 with CI [0,0], pen_ratio 0.69x, fs_nemf 0.80x, skate_ratio 0.72x, interior_jerk 0.84x (all SIG better), pene_pct_scene 0.98x / contact_count 1.02x / goal_height_err 1.01x / pene_sum_mean_floorexcl 1.68x all ns. On interactive 245 the gaps concentrate: boundary_jerk 1.85x, jerk_ratio 1.83x, fs_nemf 1.24x (WORSE than GT, the opposite sign to walk's 0.80x), goal_height_err_m 1.20x, success_last_10cm 0.9592. So the all-375 fs_nemf 1.00x 'ns' is two opposing effects cancelling. Locomotion is at or above ground truth; the remaining deficit is interactive motion — sitting, lying, manipulation — and it concentrates in seam jerk and foot skate. Note also is_object is identically 0 on all 375 LINGO sequences, so it is NOT the interactive/walk discriminator; caption=='walk' is.

use_object_keypoints: false
