human_only_ratio: 0.4
lingo_scene_num: 111
lingo_data_ratio: 1.0
empty_omomo_scene: false
random_seed: 42

scene_type: occ_temp
temp_voxel_num: 3
w: 1
guidance_weight: 1
use_guidance: false
sample_type: consistency
timing_warmup_sequences: 5

# Opt-in motion export.  When false nothing is written beyond
# evaluation/per_sequence_metrics.json and that payload carries no
# motion_export key, so an export-capable build reproduces a pre-export payload
# byte for byte.  When true, motion/<sequence_id>.npz is written next to it with
# global_jpos at the rollout rate (fps = fps / interp_s) for the frozen
# text-motion evaluator, plus the SMPL-X FK inputs so a later metric
# redefinition is a CPU rebuild instead of another GPU run.
export_motion: false

lingo_hsi_mode: ground_truth
lingo_sequence_limit: null

# Episode sharding for the quality pass.  shard_count=1 is the serial protocol
# and is the default; >1 splits the canonical episode enumeration by greedy
# longest-first bin packing over per-episode window counts, and invalidates
# every timing aggregate because the shards contend for the host.
shard_index: 0
shard_count: 1

# Serial latency pass.  Selects a deterministic scene-spanning episode subset
# sized by window budget; requires shard_count=1 so timing stays valid.
# 70 windows = 19 episodes over 18 of the 26 scenes; after the 5 warmup episodes
# that leaves 48 timed windows, i.e. ~47 min of measured guided-diffusion
# sampling at the measured 59.1 s/window (~68 min of total run wall clock).
latency_subset: false
latency_target_windows: 70

# lingo_hsi_mode=merge_shards inputs.  merge_shard_dir defaults to the parent
# directory the sharded runs wrote into; the expected totals are the full
# protocol and are the external anchor against a silently short merge.
merge_shard_dir: null
merge_expected_episodes: 375
merge_expected_windows: 2271
# 2026-08-18: default moved from `data/lingo_hsi_test/data` (v1) to v2. In v1
# `pelvis_goal` was the last frame of the FIRST 16-frame window, held fixed for
# the whole rollout, so start->goal was <= 0.778 m over all 375 episodes and the
# 0.8 m lookahead in `sample_step` clamped on every window of every episode
# (measured 0/2271 unclamped). v2 sets the goal to the rollout terminus; GT then
# scores `last_dist` == 0. The four sealed model cells and every
# `results/lingo_hsi/ground_truth*` row except `ground-truth-v2`/`-v3` predate
# this and were run against v1 -- reproduce those with an explicit
# `lingo_episode_dir=${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/data/lingo_hsi_test/data` override.
lingo_episode_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/data/lingo_hsi_test_v2/data
lingo_mesh_root: /data/yujinlun/datasets/LINGO/Scene_mesh
lingo_output_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/lingo_hsi/${lingo_hsi_mode}-${sample_type}-${oc.select:use_guidance,false}
ckpt_path: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/checkpoint/checkpoint.pth
# When null, the evaluator uses the checkpoint file stem.
model_name: null
smplx_batch_size: 128

hydra:
  run:
    dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/.claude/scratch/hydra_lingo_hsi

hypothesis: Phase 1C gate reading: C v2 + guided, the ONLY cell this branch evaluates under the user's 2026-08-18 protocol (train the full diffusion model, distil, evaluate distilled+guided — reproducing InfBaGel itself, since distillation is required and guidance is the author's own code). Checkpoint hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2_epoch089.pth (f1c09c24), distilled from B v2 epoch222 (5daaf813) after four defect repairs: 3ded4eb (rotation and joint channels 90 deg apart, so loss_fk scored a skeleton displaced 0.5578 m), a4c979c (joint channel normalized with OMOMO's constants and denormalized with LINGO's, up to 1.0263 m round-trip, which also mis-centred the scene-occupancy query and compressed every model-side world skeleton ~0.4x horizontally in both evaluators), bcb4ad4 (mask_fk computed but never applied in p_losses), eb5bc1b (loss_w_fk 50 -> 3, where 50 alone drove predicted root attitude to 122.48 deg). Full 375-episode protocol, shard_count=1 serial on one GPU so FPS stays valid, seed 42, export_motion=true, v2 episodes, paired against results/lingo_hsi/ground-truth-v3. The unguided column and the B-versus-C pre/post-distillation comparison are deliberately not run. The Phase 1C gate THRESHOLD remains deferred by the user; this row reports the reading, not a pass/fail against a number.
next_action: The gate reading is complete and the representation repair is confirmed end to end. Next work is model-side, not repair: the deficit is interactive motion, where boundary_jerk is 1.85x GT and fs_nemf 1.24x, while walk is already at or above GT. Attack seam continuity at the third derivative — transition_distance_aligned is already 0.87x GT on interactive, so the seam does not jump in position and the target is high-frequency jitter, which makes a smoothness or overlap-blending change the natural first lever rather than more budget. Do NOT re-run the unguided or B columns; the user judged a second full comparison not worth its cost. Two open items carried forward. First, loss_w_fk 3 is measured far better than 50 but is not derived-optimal: gradient parity against loss_jrot is 1.09 and the aligned-signal break-even 16.1, and neither was trained — revisit only if end-effector precision becomes the binding gap, which this reading does not show. Second, the health checks left a real residual the aggregate metrics do not surface: pelvis up-axis p95 is 73.5 deg against GT 23.8, so roughly 5% of frames still have a tipped root, and the joint channel is still not a rigid skeleton (20 of 21 bones above CV 1e-2, though the gross 3.93x pelvis-to-spine1 error is gone at 0.99x GT). Three design priors remain registered and unfixed by choice, all candidates for deliberate later change: norm.npy leaves 12.52% of windows with a vertical value below -1; its horizontal axes occupy only +/-0.436 and +/-0.422 of [-1,1], pricing horizontal error at 1/3 of height error on a locomotion corpus; and 16 of 232 channels carry an exactly constant target under lingo_only. The Phase 1C gate threshold is still deferred by the user and must be set before this row can be called a pass. The matching window_codec.py and mask_fk changes still have to land on phase/01b-hoi; handover at /data/yujinlun/report/.

global_jpos.note: dataset channel order, no re-indexing and no SMPL-X FK; slots 24-27 are SMPL-X 25/34/40/49 (index1/ring1) as in the frozen evaluator's training bundle, not SMPLX_JOINTS_28's middle1

smplx.note: schema 2 onward both arms share one SMPL-X parameter frame -- the frame human_joints_aligned.npy is stored in -- and smplx_output_transform is always 'identity', so the rebuild above needs no per-arm branch; a schema-1 generated-arm file instead needs transl replaced by zup_to_yup(transl) and its recorded 'zup_to_yup' output transform ignored
smplx.rebuild: pose = concatenate([global_orient[:, None], body_pose], axis=1); vertices, joints28 = run_smplx_model(pose, transl, betas, gender, joints_ind=SMPLX_JOINTS_28).  Wrap with StitchedSequence(frames, seams=seams*interp_scale, window_lengths=window_lengths*interp_scale, history_frames=history_frames*interp_scale) to recompute seam metrics.

rds.skipped_reason: guidance pulls joints toward free voxels regardless of need_scene, so a guided null-scene rollout is confounded; RDS is scoped to unguided cells

conclusion: 375/375, schema_version 4, finite_motion 375/375, 1 h 04 m serial single-GPU wall clock, timing_valid TRUE (per_window_wall_seconds 1.6585, aggregate_fps 25.92, rtf 0.8640 -- this operating point is real time). ANCHOR: bitwise identical to the 4-shard diagnostic cell c_guided_endpi_fix across all 375 episodes and 18,375 numeric values, 0 mismatches, which simultaneously proves 4-way episode sharding is neutral at FULL scale (the prior control covered only 93 episodes), proves commit 482a03d changed no behaviour, and carries every number already analysed off the diagnostic cell onto this official row. THE PREDICTION HELD IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Posture, the failure the three metric sections cannot see: sit/lie 117 terminal pelvis height 0.7810 -> 0.5205 (GT 0.4792) and minimum 0.7670 -> 0.5103 (GT 0.4742); stand-up 20 terminal 0.5272 -> 0.7227 (GT 0.7572); kneel/squat 3 minimum 0.9430 -> 0.6308 (GT 0.4991). The four control groups that must not move stay within 0.012 m: walk 130, standing manipulation 97, already seated 8, and stand-up minimum. Per-window, divergence is now confined to windows 1-3 (+0.082/+0.193/+0.085) against the pre-fix +0.332/+0.391 at windows 2-3, i.e. the descent now happens, about one window late. TEXT-MOTION IS THE LARGEST WIN AND WAS NOT PREDICTED IN SIZE: interactive 245 FID 91.28 [78.62, 107.29] -> 20.13 [14.48, 28.45], deduplicated gallery-32 R-Precision@1 0.1161 [0.0759, 0.1607] -> 0.2857 [0.2277, 0.3438] (Real 0.4688, so the model now recovers 61% of the evaluator's own capability against 25% before), R@2 0.1964 -> 0.3973, R@3 0.2054 -> 0.4598, MM-Dist 14.070 [13.392, 14.728] -> 8.046 [7.226, 8.875] (Real 4.419, shuffled floor 15.761), Diversity 9.70 -> 12.71 toward Real 14.89. All 375: FID 10.93 [7.93, 15.79], R@1 0.2699, MM-Dist 5.414. These are non-overlapping one-sample CIs, not a paired test between the two runs; the runner is one-sample by construction. GEOMETRY, 10,000x stratified paired bootstrap vs ground-truth-v3, seed 42, strata walk 130 / interactive 245. WALK IS ESSENTIALLY SOLVED and beats ground truth on most columns: fs_nemf 0.3457 vs 0.4082 (SIG 0.847x), pen_ratio 0.675x, skate_ratio 0.747x, transition_distance_aligned 0.832x, interior_jerk 0.870x, time_to_goal_10cm_s 0.325x, success_last_10cm identical to GT at 1.0, pene_pct_scene ns. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE INTERACTIVE SEAM: boundary_jerk 176.81 vs 77.47 (SIG 2.282x) while interior_jerk is ns 1.044x -- within-window smoothness is fine and the defect is strictly at the autoregressive seam, on exactly the 245 episodes that now really perform the posture change. Also worse on interactive: jerk_ratio 2.007x, pene_sum_mean_floorexcl 1.670x, fs_nemf 1.453x, goal_planar_err_m 0.0777 m against a constructed GT of 0. Versus the pre-fix row the trade is explicit and causal: goal_height_err_m 1.120x -> 1.021x, interior_jerk leaves 'significantly better than GT' 0.892x for ns 0.974x (it was smooth because nothing moved), success_min_10cm now identical to GT; paid for with boundary_jerk 1.597x -> 1.883x and fs_nemf ns 0.998x -> SIG 1.123x. A body that actually sits down produces seam jerk; one standing next to the chair does not. goal_orientation_err_rad is None on all 375 in both this run and ground truth -- an unpopulated key, not a defect of this run.

config.content:
defaults:
  - _self_
  - dataset: lingo_v3_test
  - guidance:
      - pelvis
  - model:
      - infbagel
  - sampler:
      - pelvis

exp_name: lingo-hsi-eval
seed: 42
train: false
batch_size: 1
device: cuda:0
vis: false
start_type: stand

max_window_size: 16
auto_regre_num: 2
interp_s: 3
fps: 30.0

load_language: true
load_scene: true
load_scene_goal: true
load_pelvis_goal: true
load_object_goal: true
use_pi: true
use_random_frame_bps: false
use_object_keypoints: false
# Keep the sampler's shape-only object tensor alive for its settled occ_temp
# interface. The scene-only dataset wrapper never writes it into occupancy.
add_object_voxel: true

human_only_ratio: 0.4
lingo_scene_num: 111
lingo_data_ratio: 1.0
empty_omomo_scene: false
random_seed: 42

scene_type: occ_temp
temp_voxel_num: 3
w: 1
guidance_weight: 1
use_guidance: false
sample_type: consistency
timing_warmup_sequences: 5

# Opt-in motion export.  When false nothing is written beyond
# evaluation/per_sequence_metrics.json and that payload carries no
# motion_export key, so an export-capable build reproduces a pre-export payload
# byte for byte.  When true, motion/<sequence_id>.npz is written next to it with
# global_jpos at the rollout rate (fps = fps / interp_s) for the frozen
# text-motion evaluator, plus the SMPL-X FK inputs so a later metric
# redefinition is a CPU rebuild instead of another GPU run.
export_motion: false

lingo_hsi_mode: ground_truth
lingo_sequence_limit: null

# Episode sharding for the quality pass.  shard_count=1 is the serial protocol
# and is the default; >1 splits the canonical episode enumeration by greedy
# longest-first bin packing over per-episode window counts, and invalidates
# every timing aggregate because the shards contend for the host.
# 2026-08-20 diagnostic gate, default OFF so the sealed path is bitwise unchanged.
# test_infbagel_hosi.sample_step zeroes `pi` inside `if is_loco:` but leaves `end_pi`,
# so the model receives end_pi - pi = 42*step + 48 while training carries
# min(pi + 16*3, seq_len) i.e. exactly 48 on 517,484 of 529,132 need_pi windows.
# Only step 0 is training-legal: 375 of 2271 eval windows (16.5%).
# true = keep the true pi, restoring end_pi - pi == 48 on every window.
hsi_progress_fix: false

# 2026-08-20 diagnostic gates on the per-window pelvis goal, both default to the
# CURRENT behaviour so every sealed cell stays bitwise reproducible.
#
# Training (datasets/infbagel.py:468-477) feeds pelvis_goal = joints[w0+45, 0] with
# y=0 for both the sit/lie and loco branches -- a per-window target.  The driver
# instead takes a point `hsi_lookahead_m` ahead along _straight_trajectory(), a
# straight chord from episode start to episode goal.  Measured distance from the
# driver's choice to training's target, over all 2271 windows:
#   walk 1099 windows: 1.0180 m mean (straight chord) vs 0.2124 m (GT pelvis path)
#   sit/lie 609      : 0.2012 m                       vs 0.1643 m
# and the GT pelvis advances only 0.478 m (walk) / 0.186 m (sit/lie) over those 45
# raw frames, against a hardcoded 0.8 m.  On a real wiggly path 0.8 m of ARC length
# nets ~0.48 m of displacement, so the constant is arc-length-calibrated; the chord
# makes arc length equal displacement, so it overshoots ~1.7x on walk.
# Evidence: .claude/scratch/isloco_offline_20260820/{goal_source_error.py,controls.py}
#
# hsi_gt_trajectory: true = build the lookahead path from the episode's GROUND-TRUTH
#   pelvis xz path instead of the chord.  Attribution UPPER BOUND only -- it feeds
#   privileged information a deployment cannot have.  Never use it for a baseline.
hsi_gt_trajectory: false
# hsi_lookahead_m: the lookahead arc length in metres.  0.8 is the released value.
#   0.48 is the deployable variant: one global constant, no privileged information.
hsi_lookahead_m: 0.8

shard_index: 0
shard_count: 1

# Serial latency pass.  Selects a deterministic scene-spanning episode subset
# sized by window budget; requires shard_count=1 so timing stays valid.
# 70 windows = 19 episodes over 18 of the 26 scenes; after the 5 warmup episodes
# that leaves 48 timed windows, i.e. ~47 min of measured guided-diffusion
# sampling at the measured 59.1 s/window (~68 min of total run wall clock).
latency_subset: false
latency_target_windows: 70

# lingo_hsi_mode=merge_shards inputs.  merge_shard_dir defaults to the parent
# directory the sharded runs wrote into; the expected totals are the full
# protocol and are the external anchor against a silently short merge.
merge_shard_dir: null
merge_expected_episodes: 375
merge_expected_windows: 2271
# 2026-08-18: default moved from `data/lingo_hsi_test/data` (v1) to v2. In v1
# `pelvis_goal` was the last frame of the FIRST 16-frame window, held fixed for
# the whole rollout, so start->goal was <= 0.778 m over all 375 episodes and the
# 0.8 m lookahead in `sample_step` clamped on every window of every episode
# (measured 0/2271 unclamped). v2 sets the goal to the rollout terminus; GT then
# scores `last_dist` == 0. The four sealed model cells and every
# `results/lingo_hsi/ground_truth*` row except `ground-truth-v2`/`-v3` predate
# this and were run against v1 -- reproduce those with an explicit
# `lingo_episode_dir=${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/data/lingo_hsi_test/data` override.
lingo_episode_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/data/lingo_hsi_test_v2/data
lingo_mesh_root: /data/yujinlun/datasets/LINGO/Scene_mesh
lingo_output_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/lingo_hsi/${lingo_hsi_mode}-${sample_type}-${oc.select:use_guidance,false}
ckpt_path: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/checkpoint/checkpoint.pth
# When null, the evaluator uses the checkpoint file stem.
model_name: null
smplx_batch_size: 128

hydra:
  run:
    dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/.claude/scratch/hydra_lingo_hsi

hypothesis: The pre-fix eval operating point zeroed pi inside 'if is_loco:' and left end_pi, so 1896 of 2271 windows (83.5%) received end_pi - pi = 42*step + 48 while training carries exactly 48 on 517,484 of 529,132 need_pi windows. Restoring the true pi (hsi_progress_fix=true) is the correct baseline operating point. Prediction: the geometric columns get WORSE where the pre-fix row was flattered by a body that never performed the vertical posture change, and the posture and text-motion columns get better. The two trajectory alternatives were already measured and rejected, so hsi_gt_trajectory=false and hsi_lookahead_m=0.8 (the released chord) stand.
next_action: This row is the registered HSI baseline; report tables should cite it instead of p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-s42-20260820, which measured a driver defect. Next model-side iteration direction is interactive boundary_jerk (176.81 vs GT 77.47 on the 245), recorded per the user's instruction and NOT acted on here. Immediately next is the approved C v3 re-distillation: cfg_scale_embedding was frozen throughout the B->C lineage (verified from B's checkpoint bytes -- weight RMS 1.002e-04 exactly at its std=1e-4 init and bias L2 exactly 0.0 after 222 epochs), so C has no continuous-w capability at all and only the w=-1 sentinel works. Phase 1C's gate threshold remains the user's to set.

global_jpos.note: dataset channel order, no re-indexing and no SMPL-X FK; slots 24-27 are SMPL-X 25/34/40/49 (index1/ring1) as in the frozen evaluator's training bundle, not SMPLX_JOINTS_28's middle1

motion_export.layout: one non-pickle NPZ per sequence under motion/<sequence_id>.npz

smplx.note: schema 2 onward both arms share one SMPL-X parameter frame -- the frame human_joints_aligned.npy is stored in -- and smplx_output_transform is always 'identity', so the rebuild above needs no per-arm branch; a schema-1 generated-arm file instead needs transl replaced by zup_to_yup(transl) and its recorded 'zup_to_yup' output transform ignored
smplx.rebuild: pose = concatenate([global_orient[:, None], body_pose], axis=1); vertices, joints28 = run_smplx_model(pose, transl, betas, gender, joints_ind=SMPLX_JOINTS_28).  Wrap with StitchedSequence(frames, seams=seams*interp_scale, window_lengths=window_lengths*interp_scale, history_frames=history_frames*interp_scale) to recompute seam metrics.

rds.skipped_reason: guidance pulls joints toward free voxels regardless of need_scene, so a guided null-scene rollout is confounded; RDS is scoped to unguided cells

conclusion: ABORTED at optimizer update 2688 of 58,678 (4.6%, 30 min of a projected 10.28 h at the measured 1.585 updates/s). Stopped on evidence against the registered predecessor, not on a threshold guess. C v2 over its ENTIRE 58,678-update run has grad-norm median 0.079029, p99 0.37621, max 0.89946, and ZERO values above 20x its own median. C v3 at update 2688 had block median 1.5528 (19.7x v2's whole-run median) and max 19.954 (22.2x v2's whole-run maximum), inside the first 4.6% of training, with the median still climbing from 0.97348 (updates 2000-2499) to 1.5528 (2500-2999) AFTER warmup ended at 2000 and lr became constant. No gradient clipping exists in this loop and run B has two recorded unclipped loss-spike events. THE LOSS ALONE WAS AMBIGUOUS AND MUST NOT BE CITED AS THE REASON: v3's loss rose 34x from 0.00114 to 0.0391 over the same window where v2 stayed flat at ~0.00105, but that rise is partly EXPECTED, because v2's target was w-invariant so the student could satisfy the consistency condition without representing any w dependence, whereas fix 2 makes the target w-dependent and raises the achievable floor. The rise tracked the lr ramp exactly and then flattened (last two blocks 1.001x). The gradient norm is what is decisive. MECHANISM MEASURED FROM CHECKPOINT BYTES, NOT INFERRED: cfg_scale_embedding.proj.weight L2 is 0.0513026 in B epoch222 and 0.0513026 in the registered C v2 epoch089 -- byte-identical, RMS 1.002e-04 exactly its nn.init.normal_(std=1e-4), bias L2 exactly 0.0, which independently confirms from the far end of the lineage that the module never trained in v2. In v3 that same weight reached 0.388893 (7.58x) within epoch 0 alone, while lr was still ramping at about 6e-05, and the bias came off zero to 0.012948. Adam is scale-invariant so each element moves about lr per step regardless of gradient magnitude, the module starts three orders of magnitude below a functional scale, and update_ema at 0.95 copies it into the target with roughly a 20-step lag, so the student chases a target whose w dependence is itself moving fast with nothing pinning the scale or bounding the gradient. MY LAUNCH DECISION WAS WRONG AND THE PREFLIGHT WAS RIGHT: the preflight flagged this exact risk and proposed a separate lower-lr param group or clipping; I overruled it on the grounds that downstream LayerNorm bounds the module's influence (measured: multiplying the weight by 1000 moves the target output 0.479 relative, not 479x) and that slowing the module that must travel furthest would recreate the failure being fixed. The first argument was wrong in a way that measurement did not cover -- LayerNorm bounds the magnitude of the effect on the output, not the gradient into an unconstrained parameter nor the rate at which its motion moves the EMA-coupled target. The second argument still holds, which is why the remedy is a user decision and not an obvious lr cut. The three fixes themselves remain correct and committed at eb2e4486 with a passing preflight; what is missing is a mechanism to bound the resulting motion.

config.content:
# Model C: consistency-model distillation from run B, LINGO-only HSI.
#
# Author CM procedure (config_train_infbagel_cm.yaml): sample_type consistency,
# load_state_dict true from the teacher's FINAL-epoch checkpoint, loss_w_fk 1 /
# loss_w_obj_pts 0.5, is_mix false on both the model and the sampler.
# Run B data/scene settings unchanged.  Budget invariant is processed windows,
# per docs/plan/PHASE_1C_HSI.md 2026-08-13 section 3: 58,678 optimizer updates.
defaults:
  - dataset: lingo_v3_train
  - guidance:
      - pelvis
  - model:
      - infbagel
  - sampler:
      - pelvis
  - _self_

# _v3: results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2/ backs registered row
# p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-v2-s42-20260819 and its epoch089 checkpoint backs the
# registered baseline p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-progressfix-s42-20260821,
# so neither may be overwritten. (v1 likewise backs p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-s42-20260816.)
#
# v3 re-distills because `cfg_scale_embedding` was never trainable anywhere in the
# B->C lineage, so C has no continuous-w capability -- only the w=-1 sentinel works
# and `w: 1` below is decorative. Measured from B's checkpoint bytes: after 222
# epochs the weight RMS is 1.002e-04, exactly its nn.init.normal_(std=1e-4), and the
# bias L2 is exactly 0.0. Three coupled fixes, none sufficient alone:
#   train_infbagel.py  -- unfreeze student_model.module.cfg_scale_embedding; it is a
#                         SIBLING of the four unfrozen blocks, so requires_grad_(False)
#                         over the whole model was never revoked for it.
#   models/infbagel.py -- pass cfg_scale=w to the target; without it the regression
#                         target is w-invariant and pushes the newly trainable
#                         embedding back to zero. It also moves the target off the
#                         `else:` branch's random 10% scene ablation onto the same
#                         per-row cfg_scale == -1 mask the student uses.
#   train_infbagel.py  -- teacher and target .eval(); init_model ends in .train(), so
#                         the distillation target carried live dropout.
# Preflight: .claude/scratch/cv3_smoke_20260821/smoke_report.txt (A/B/C/D all PASS,
# with pre-fix controls of grad=None and a bitwise-zero w response).
exp_name: hsi_c_lingo_cm_v3
seed: 42
random_seed: 42
sample_type: consistency
lingo_scene_num: 45
lingo_data_ratio: 0.5
empty_omomo_scene: false
epochs: 90
ckpt_interval: 20
lingo_only: true

train: true
load_state_dict: true
batch_size: 512
effective_batch_size: 2048
gradient_accumulation_steps: 1
precision: bf16_tf32
lr: 0.0002
warmup_updates: 2000
device: cuda:0
use_tensorboard: true
save_checkpoints: true
max_optimizer_updates: 58678
benchmark_metrics_path: null
exp_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/${exp_name}

w: 1

num_gpus: 4
num_workers: 2
scene_type: occ_temp
max_window_size: 16
vis: false
start_type: stand

load_language: true
load_scene: true
use_pi: true
load_scene_goal: true
load_pelvis_goal: true
load_object_goal: true

human_only_ratio: 0.4

temp_voxel_num: 3

use_random_frame_bps: true
use_object_keypoints: true
add_object_voxel: true

loss_w_obj_pts: 0.5
loss_w_fk: 1
auto_regre_num: 2

start_epoch: 0
# Teacher is the post-fix B, not the pre-fix one. Distilling from the old
# checkpoint would faithfully preserve its 122 deg rotation channel.
# loss_w_fk stays 1 here: consistency_loss is one term over all 232 channels
# against the teacher, so there is no loss_jrot to starve, and 1 already sits
# below B's measured 1.09 rotation-channel gradient parity. See the A/B recorded
# in config_train_hsi_b_lingo_full.yaml.
ckpt_path: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/hsi_b_lingo_full_v2/checkpoints/hsi_b_lingo_full_v2_epoch222.pth
resume_from: ""

hydra:
  run:
    dir: ${exp_dir}

hypothesis: C has no continuous-w capability because cfg_scale_embedding was never trainable anywhere in the B->C lineage. Three coupled fixes (unfreeze the module in the student, pass cfg_scale=w to the target, .eval() teacher and target) restore it, and the resulting run should otherwise behave like C v2, whose config, data and schedule are unchanged.
next_action: User decision on how to bound the motion before relaunching under a NEW run id. Candidates, none implemented: (1) finite-max_norm gradient clipping, which is the least targeted and most principled -- v2's whole-run p99 of 0.376 and max of 0.899 mean a max_norm near 1.0 would be a no-op for v2-like dynamics while bounding v3's tail, and it addresses the unclipped half of B's known spike history; note the existing comment at the log_grad_norm site warns only against max_norm=inf, a finite value is safe. (2) A saner initialisation for cfg_scale_embedding.proj than std=1e-4, which removes the REASON for three orders of magnitude of travel; the 1e-4 init is defensible only for a module that is never trained. (3) A separate lower-lr param group or a longer per-module warmup, targeted but arbitrary in its constant and carrying the risk that the module never becomes functional. Options 1 and 2 are complementary. Any of them expands the change set beyond the three authorised fixes, which is why this stopped here. The registered HSI baseline p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-progressfix-s42-20260821 is unaffected and remains the reference row.

results.abort_reason: Gradient-norm divergence against the registered predecessor. Stopped on evidence, not on a threshold guess. Run C v2, same config, same data, same schedule, differing only by the three cfg_scale_embedding fixes, has over its ENTIRE 58,678-update run a grad-norm median of 0.079029, p99 0.37621, max 0.89946, and ZERO values above 20x its own median. C v3 at update 2688 had a block median of 1.5528 (19.7x v2's whole-run median) and a max of 19.954 (22.2x v2's whole-run maximum), reached inside the first 4.6% of training, and the median was still climbing (0.97348 over updates 2000-2499 to 1.5528 over 2500-2999) after warmup ended at update 2000 and lr became constant. There is no gradient clipping in this training loop, and run B has a recorded history of two unclipped loss-spike events.
results.checkpoint_written: hsi_c_lingo_cm_v3_epoch000.pth (epoch 0, 656 optimizer updates); no usable model
results.fixes_remain_committed: eb2e448641debccc8789b340afe3a11586e3cc15. The three fixes are correct and their preflight (.claude/scratch/cv3_smoke_20260821/smoke_report.txt) passed A/B/C/D with pre-fix controls of grad=None and a bitwise-zero w response. What is missing is a mechanism to bound the resulting motion.

loss_trace_vs_v2.note: Medians of 200-step blocks of the per-rank printed loss. v2 is flat at its degenerate initialisation value because its target was w-INVARIANT, so the student could satisfy the consistency condition without representing any w dependence. v3's rise is therefore partly EXPECTED: fix 2 makes the target w-dependent, so the achievable loss floor is genuinely higher. The rise tracked the lr ramp exactly and then flattened. The loss alone is thus ambiguous; the grad norm is what is decisive.

mechanism_measured_not_inferred.reading: C v2's module is byte-identical to B's, at RMS 1.002e-04 exactly its nn.init.normal_(std=1e-4) with a bias of exactly 0.0 -- independent end-of-lineage confirmation that the module never trained in v2, which is the defect v3 set out to fix. In v3 the same weight grew 7.58x within epoch 0 alone, while lr was still ramping through warmup at about 6e-05. Adam is scale-invariant, so each element moves about lr per step regardless of gradient size, and the module starts three orders of magnitude below a functional scale. update_ema at rate 0.95 then copies it into the target with roughly a 20-step lag, so the student is chasing a target whose w dependence is itself moving fast, and nothing in the loop pins the scale or bounds the gradient.

results.what_was_wrong_in_the_launch_decision: The preflight subagent flagged exactly this risk before launch and proposed a separate lower-lr param group or clipping for this module. I overruled it, arguing that downstream LayerNorm bounds the module's influence (measured: multiplying the weight by 1000 changes the target output by 0.479 relative, not 479x) and that lowering the lr of the one module that must travel furthest would recreate the failure being fixed. The first argument was wrong in a way the measurement did not cover: LayerNorm bounds the MAGNITUDE of the module's effect on the output, not the gradient flowing into an unconstrained parameter driven by a scale-invariant optimizer, nor the rate at which that motion moves the EMA-coupled target. The second argument still stands on its own, which is why the remedy is a decision for the user rather than an obvious lr reduction.

conclusion: SPLIT RESULT. Training health and teacher fidelity: PASS. 58,678 updates, exit 0, 10.69 h, zero non-finite in 234,712 gradient records and every cfg diagnostic field; clipping engaged on 0 of 234,712 records (coefficient min exactly 1.0) with post-warmup norm median 0.0836 and max 0.5963, below v2 own 0.89946; max adjacent loss ratio 1.278 against v2 1.628; epoch-30-onward loss median 0.00087, equal to v2, with a 2.03x lower maximum. Open risk 1 is CLOSED and benign: drift away from the teacher decelerated and saturated, the per-1k-update rate falling ~70x from epoch000-020 to epoch020-040 and turning slightly negative over the final epochs, landing at 0.98469x v2 vs teacher and 0.99630x vs GT -- marginally better than v2, not worse. Open risk 2 is CLOSED NEGATIVE: continuous-w direction never consolidated. Cosines at w=0/2/4 went from +0.1464/+0.1094/+0.0160 at update 3,000 to +0.0902/-0.0293/+0.0031 at epoch089 (ddim index 2; same verdict at index 20), with w=2 -- in-distribution, since training draws w uniform on [0, w_max=2.0) -- turning NEGATIVE. Response magnitude is 49-65x v2, but magnitude is explicitly not a health signal: the collapsed arms raised it up to 67x at near-zero cosine. Sentinel cosine +0.7126 sits far above the collapsed band 0.3007-0.3524 but does not beat v2 +0.7427, though v4 sentinel MAGNITUDE 0.44002 is closer to the theoretical 0.50040 than v2 0.36531. Mechanism for the null: w reaches the objective only through x_prev, the DDIM step from the teacher CFG-extrapolated prediction, and the CFG direction is 1.03-1.13 pct of the conditional prediction magnitude at every probed timestep, so the objective prices continuous-w direction at roughly one percent of the signal. Unfreezing the embedding made the response large; it did not make the objective supervise its direction. Therefore cfg.w remains decorative and only the w=-1 sentinel works -- the same standing as v2 -- and the eleven-line v3 attribution holds: the v3 collapse was the teacher/target .eval() alone, with the cfg learning rate exonerated by a 200x sweep. Bitwise continuity: epoch000 is bit-identical to the approved precheck checkpoint and the first 1024 gradient records matched it 1024/1024, so the precheck evidence applies to this run literally.

# Model C: consistency-model distillation from run B, LINGO-only HSI.
#
# Author CM procedure (config_train_infbagel_cm.yaml): sample_type consistency,
# load_state_dict true from the teacher's FINAL-epoch checkpoint, loss_w_fk 1 /
# loss_w_obj_pts 0.5, is_mix false on both the model and the sampler.
# Run B data/scene settings unchanged.  Budget invariant is processed windows,
# per docs/plan/PHASE_1C_HSI.md 2026-08-13 section 3: 58,678 optimizer updates.
defaults:
  - dataset: lingo_v3_train
  - guidance:
      - pelvis
  - model:
      - infbagel
  - sampler:
      - pelvis
  - _self_

# _v4: three earlier directories are protected. results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2/ backs
# registered row p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-v2-s42-20260819 and its epoch089 checkpoint backs
# the registered baseline p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-progressfix-s42-20260821;
# results/hsi_c_lingo_cm/ backs p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-s42-20260816; results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v3/
# backs the aborted manifest p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-v3-s42-20260821. None may be overwritten.
#
# C is re-distilled because `cfg_scale_embedding` was never trainable anywhere in the
# B->C lineage, so C has no continuous-w capability. Measured from B's checkpoint
# bytes: after 222 epochs the weight RMS is 1.002e-04, exactly its
# nn.init.normal_(std=1e-4), and the bias L2 is exactly 0.0. Training draws w per row
# in sample_cfg_scale_mixed -- 10 pct at exactly -1.0, 90 pct uniform on [0, w_max=2.0)
# -- so only the w=-1 sentinel path ever worked and the distilled range is [0, 2].
#
# v3 shipped three coupled changes and collapsed by update 656. Two 1312-update
# single-revert arms attributed the collapse to the third one alone:
#   KEPT       train_infbagel.py  -- unfreeze student_model.module.cfg_scale_embedding.
#              It is a SIBLING of the four unfrozen blocks, so requires_grad_(False)
#              over the whole model was never revoked for it.
#   KEPT       models/infbagel.py -- pass cfg_scale=w to the target. Without it the
#              regression target is w-invariant and drives the newly trainable
#              embedding back to zero; it also moves the target off the `else:`
#              branch's random 10 pct scene ablation onto the same per-row
#              cfg_scale == -1 mask the student uses. Reverting only this still
#              collapsed: 0.434 vs-GT error at update 1312 against v2's 0.058.
#   RETRACTED  train_infbagel.py  -- teacher and target .eval(). This was the entire
#              collapse. update_ema(rate=0.95) has a ~13.5-update half-life, so the
#              target is nearly the student itself, the consistency condition is
#              near-degenerate, and the target's dropout is what breaks the
#              degeneracy. There is no BatchNorm anywhere in code/models/, so .eval()
#              changed nothing else. Reverting only this recovered fully, with fixes 1
#              and 2 still active: loss within 1 pct of v2 at every block and fidelity
#              0.7 pct better than v2 at update 656.
#
# One Adam parameter group at lr 2e-4 with the original warmup: the cfg-embedding
# learning rate is exonerated. A 200x sweep {1e-6, 4e-6, 1e-5} against the 2e-4 arm
# agreed within 0.4 pct on vs-GT error at update 656 and all four sat at 2.86x v2, so
# the lr was never the variable; and the revert-fix-3 arm ran the embedding at the
# full 2e-4, reached 16.1x its init RMS, and kept a flat loss.
#
# Preflight: .claude/scratch/cv3_smoke_20260821/smoke_report.txt (A/B/C/D all PASS).
# Attribution and the 3000-update v4 precheck: docs/plan/PHASE_1C_HSI.md, 2026-08-21
# section.
exp_name: hsi_c_lingo_cm_v4
seed: 42
random_seed: 42
sample_type: consistency
lingo_scene_num: 45
lingo_data_ratio: 0.5
empty_omomo_scene: false
epochs: 90
ckpt_interval: 20
lingo_only: true

train: true
load_state_dict: true
batch_size: 512
effective_batch_size: 2048
gradient_accumulation_steps: 1
precision: bf16_tf32
lr: 0.0002
warmup_updates: 2000
# Insurance, not a tuned threshold, and measured inert on both trajectories: v2's
# pre-clip global norm never exceeded 0.89946 across all 234,712 records of its full
# run, and the v4 precheck peaked at 0.53411 with the clip engaging on 0 of 3000
# updates. It exists to bound a divergence event that cannot be predicted, which is
# how v3 burned 2688 updates. The logged norm stays PRE-clip so it remains comparable
# with v2 and with every unclipped run before it.
grad_clip_max_norm: 1.0
# Per-update cfg_scale_embedding instrument: pre-clip trunk/cfg gradient split, clip
# coefficient, weight/bias RMS, relative step size, and student-to-EMA-target
# distance. Costs +3.4 pct per update (0.65570 vs 0.63072 s measured at u2751-3000),
# i.e. 10.28 h -> 10.69 h, and it is the only channel that can see the two open risks
# in this recipe: cfg RMS growth and drift away from the teacher.
log_cfg_embedding_diagnostics: true
device: cuda:0
use_tensorboard: true
save_checkpoints: true
max_optimizer_updates: 58678
benchmark_metrics_path: null
exp_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/${exp_name}

w: 1

num_gpus: 4
num_workers: 2
scene_type: occ_temp
max_window_size: 16
vis: false
start_type: stand

load_language: true
load_scene: true
use_pi: true
load_scene_goal: true
load_pelvis_goal: true
load_object_goal: true

human_only_ratio: 0.4

temp_voxel_num: 3

use_random_frame_bps: true
use_object_keypoints: true
add_object_voxel: true

loss_w_obj_pts: 0.5
loss_w_fk: 1
auto_regre_num: 2

start_epoch: 0
# Teacher is the post-fix B, not the pre-fix one. Distilling from the old
# checkpoint would faithfully preserve its 122 deg rotation channel.
# loss_w_fk stays 1 here: consistency_loss is one term over all 232 channels
# against the teacher, so there is no loss_jrot to starve, and 1 already sits
# below B's measured 1.09 rotation-channel gradient parity. See the A/B recorded
# in config_train_hsi_b_lingo_full.yaml.
ckpt_path: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/hsi_b_lingo_full_v2/checkpoints/hsi_b_lingo_full_v2_epoch222.pth
resume_from: ""

hydra:
  run:
    dir: ${exp_dir}
overrides: objective=consistency-model distillation from run B (teacher epoch222), LINGO-only v3 train, re-distilled so cfg_scale_embedding is trainable and C gains continuous-w capability

optimizer_param_groups=1. The separate cfg_scale_embedding group used during the diagnostic phase is NOT carried forward; it was never committed. Adam is elementwise and its update rule reads only a parameter own moments plus its group scalars, so splitting one group into two with identical hyperparameters is bitwise identical -- verified, 9184 logged values over 1312 updates agree exactly between the single-group trainer and the two-group revert-fix-3 arm.

recipe_delta_vs_v2=three coupled changes were proposed; two are kept and one is RETRACTED. KEPT: unfreeze student_model.module.cfg_scale_embedding (it is a sibling of the four unfrozen blocks so requires_grad_(False) over the whole model was never revoked for it; measured from B checkpoint bytes, weight RMS after 222 epochs is 1.002e-04, exactly its nn.init.normal_(std=1e-4), and bias L2 is exactly 0.0). KEPT: models/infbagel.py passes cfg_scale=w to the EMA target, without which the regression target is w-invariant and drives the newly trainable embedding back to zero. RETRACTED: teacher and target .eval(). That single change caused the v3 collapse.

attribution_evidence=two 1312-update single-revert arms, identical in every other respect. One-step prediction relative error at t=419 on a fixed batch, all students in one probe invocation. vs-GT at update 656: v2 0.05814; all-three-changes 0.16598; revert-change-2 0.16870 (still collapses, 0.43381 by update 1312); revert-change-3 0.05774 (recovers fully, 0.06666 at update 1312, 0.7 pct BETTER than v2 at 656). Not a combination effect: reverting change 3 alone recovers while changes 1 and 2 stay active. Mechanism: update_ema(target, student, 0.95) is a ~13.5-update half-life so the EMA target is nearly the student itself and the consistency condition is near-degenerate; the target dropout is the noise that breaks the degeneracy. No BatchNorm anywhere in code/models/, so .eval() changed nothing else.

cfg_lr_exonerated=a 200x sweep of the cfg group peak lr agrees within 0.4 pct on vs-GT error at update 656 and every arm sits at 2.86x v2: 1e-6 0.16562, 4e-6 0.16619, 1e-5 0.16634, 2e-4 0.16598. The lr was never the variable. Converse: the revert-change-3 arm ran that module at the full 2e-4, reached 16.1x its init RMS, and kept a flat loss.

gradient_clipping=grad_clip_max_norm 1.0, insurance and not a tuned threshold, and measured inert on both trajectories: v2 pre-clip global norm never exceeded 0.89946 across all 234,712 records of its full run, and the v4 3000-update precheck peaked at 0.53411 with the clip engaging on 0 of 3000 updates. Comparability with v2 and with every unclipped run before it is preserved because the LOGGED norm stays pre-clip. It does not rescue a bad recipe: the three collapsed arms carried the same max_norm=1.0 and still collapsed.

instrumentation=+log_grad_norm=true plus log_cfg_embedding_diagnostics=true. The cfg instrument records pre-clip trunk/cfg gradient split, clip coefficient, weight/bias RMS, relative step size and student-to-EMA-target distance every update. Measured cost 0.63072 -> 0.65570 s/update at u2751-3000, +3.4 pct, i.e. 10.28 h -> 10.69 h. Its pre-clip ordering was corrected during the diagnostic phase: the norms were computed after the in-place clip multiply while labelled pre-clip, which under-reported the v3 trunk ratio as 6.84x when it was 9.75x.

precheck=3000 updates cold from B epoch222, results/hsi_c_cand_precheck, rc=0, zero non-finite. Fidelity 0.06434/0.07554 vs teacher/GT at t=419, better than v2 converged 0.07459/0.08464 and 17.5x better than the collapsed arm at the same update count. Block loss tracks v2 within 3 pct. Trunk gradient median 1.03x v2 (range 0.76-1.30x) and FALLING after warmup, 0.2218 -> 0.1547. cfg share of the global norm falling 0.41 -> 0.15 pct. EMA-distance/param-norm falling 0.206 -> 0.085. Adam saturation flat at 0.86x against 1.90-2.10x in the collapsed arms. w=-1 sentinel cosine +0.8687 against v2 converged +0.7427 and the collapsed band +0.3007..+0.3524. Continuous-w cosines positive at all of w=0/2/4 for the first time (+0.1464/+0.1094/+0.0160) on 57-63x larger magnitude.

open_risks=two, neither answerable at 5.1 pct of budget. (1) the candidate drifts away from the teacher faster than v2, reaching v2 update-13120 vs-teacher level by update 3000; expected in direction because change 2 makes the target w-dependent, but the landing point is unknown. (2) continuous-w cosines are positive but small. Monitoring uses cosine, clip engagement and Adam saturation -- NEVER w-response magnitude, which rose up to 67x in collapsed arms while cosine stayed near zero. Training draws w per row via sample_cfg_scale_mixed: 10 pct at exactly -1.0, 90 pct uniform on [0, w_max=2.0), so w=4 lies at twice the distilled ceiling and its weak cosine is extrapolation.

throughput_evidence=median inter-update t_mono at u2751-3000 of the 3000-update precheck at this exact 4x512xaccum1 layout with the instrument on. The same window without the cfg instrument, from v2, is 0.63072 s/update. Layout is unchanged from v1/v2: the 8x256 layout stays rejected on process-neutrality, not on speed.
cold_start=load_state_dict from the teacher, resume_from empty. Deliberately NOT resumed from the aborted v3 optimizer state.

teacher_checkpoint_sha256=5daaf813ca82878868602840760f35df43b642d73f73cb37e24bb5a4dbf62b4c, bit-identical to the teacher registered for p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-v2-s42-20260819, so C v4 vs C v2 is a clean recipe A/B

resolved_config_preflight=results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v4/preflight/config_resolved_preflight.yaml, generated at the launch commit with the exact overrides, unresolved interpolations 0, empty stderr, sha256 1bff14c4cb7adfbf4aac36f3fdd9eabc8c7b603bf57fe7d34812f87db33a92ea. is_mix=false confirmed on BOTH the model and the sampler by reading the resolved config, not inferred from defaults.
authority_suite=289 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed, run on the exact tree that was committed as 8ff078a, before this manifest

hardware_assignment_reading=hardware_assignment records the pool each expert owns; HSI owns the 8-GPU authority host and this run allocates 4 of those cards. GPUs 4-7 rather than 0-3 because 0-3 have historically belonged to another user and this run holds its cards for ~10.7 h. Physical card identity is numerically irrelevant: per-rank seeding is seed+rank and does not read the device index. experiments/training_resource_protocol.json is deliberately unamended.

protected_directories=results/hsi_c_lingo_cm (p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-s42-20260816), results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v2 (p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-v2-s42-20260819 and the epoch089 checkpoint backing p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-progressfix-s42-20260821), results/hsi_c_lingo_cm_v3 (the aborted manifest). None is overwritten; v4 is a new directory.
preregistration_commit=8ff078a (recipe + config + dated plan section, committed before this manifest)
provenance_note=git_commit is recorded at metrics-write time, so no commit may be created while this run is in flight; 8ff078a precedes the launch deliberately
gate_role=C is the Phase 1C gate, judged under guided consistency sampling; the gate threshold itself remains deferred by the user and is not defined by this run

hypothesis: Re-distilling C with cfg_scale_embedding trainable and the EMA target receiving cfg_scale=w, while teacher and target stay in train() mode, will train as healthily as v2 AND give C the continuous-w capability it has never had. Preregistered at commit 8ff078a; the two open risks carried in from the 3000-update precheck were (1) faster-than-v2 drift away from the teacher and (2) continuous-w cosines positive but small.
next_action: Do not spend further GPU time on continuous-w under this objective without changing how w is priced -- a fourth distillation at the same 1 pct signal share would be a third null. Two candidate levers, neither preregistered and both requiring the user approval: raise w_max or oversample large |w| rows so the CFG direction carries more of the objective, or add an explicit direction term on cond-uncond rather than routing w through x_prev alone. Separately and independently: v4 epoch089 is a valid gate artefact on teacher fidelity and may be evaluated under the C+guided protocol against the registered baseline p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-progressfix-s42-20260821, but since v4 matches v2 to within 1.6 pct on one-step fidelity and shares its w standing, that evaluation should be justified as a gate reading rather than as a test of the w hypothesis. gradient_norm_summary.comparison_note: v2 over its full run had median 0.0790 and max 0.89946; v4 sits in the same regime with a LOWER maximum. Both are ~75x below run B v2 post-warmup median 5.9947 on the identical host and layout, which is a property of the consistency vs diffusion objective, not a defect.

instrument_completeness.note: All 8 streams have exactly 58,678 rows, so the end-of-run tail flush lost nothing.

loss_summary.basis: rank 0, per-update, from the cfg instrument
loss_summary.note: Monotone-ish decline with no excursion. v2 epoch30-onward was median 0.000871 / max 0.002641; v4 is equal in median and has a 2.03x LOWER maximum.

results.metrics_note: Training workload only. No rollout, native-domain or gate metric is claimed by this record. Fidelity and w-response numbers here are one-step prediction probes on a fixed batch of 8 with zero is_object rows; they license no claim about rollout metrics. The C+guided evaluation is a separate record.
results.objective: consistency-model distillation from run B v2 (sample_type=consistency), re-distilled with cfg_scale_embedding trainable

objective_weights.loss_w_fk_note: Unchanged from v2. consistency_loss is a single term over all 232 channels against the EMA target, so there is no loss_jrot to be starved.
objective_weights.loss_w_obj_pts_note: Inert under lingo_only: loss_object is None at every update because mask_points is ANDed with is_object.
objective_weights.w_note: cfg.w is NOT the training w. Training draws w per row in sample_cfg_scale_mixed: 10 pct at exactly -1.0, 90 pct uniform on [0, w_max=2.0). cfg.w only affects sampling.

recipe_delta_vs_v2.kept_1: student_model.module.cfg_scale_embedding.requires_grad_(True) -- it is a sibling of the four unfrozen blocks so requires_grad_(False) over the whole model was never revoked for it
recipe_delta_vs_v2.kept_2: models/infbagel.py passes cfg_scale=w to the EMA target, so the regression target is w-dependent
recipe_delta_vs_v2.note: One Adam group at lr 2e-4 with warmup 2000. The separate cfg group used during diagnosis was never committed and is not carried forward.
recipe_delta_vs_v2.retracted_3: teacher_model.eval() / target_model.eval(). That single change caused the v3 collapse; see the 2026-08-21 plan section.

teacher.note: Bit-identical to the teacher registered for p1-hsi-c-lingo-cm-v2-s42-20260819, so C v4 vs C v2 is a clean recipe A/B with the teacher held fixed.

teacher_fidelity_probe.basis: one-step prediction relative error at ddim index 20 (t=419), w=1, fixed batch of 8, seed 42, all students in ONE probe invocation
teacher_fidelity_probe.verdict: The open risk from the precheck is CLOSED and benign. Drift away from the teacher decelerated and saturated: the per-1k-update drift rate falls ~70x from epoch000-020 to epoch020-040 and is slightly negative over the final epochs. v4 landed at 0.98469x v2 vs teacher and 0.99630x v2 vs GT -- marginally better, not worse.

w_conditioning_outcome.magnitude_note: v4 continuous-w response magnitude is 49-65x v2 (ratio-to-target 0.166-0.244 vs v2 0.003), but magnitude is explicitly NOT a health signal: in the collapsed arms magnitude rose up to 67x while cosine stayed near zero.
w_conditioning_outcome.mechanism: w enters the objective ONLY through x_prev, the DDIM step taken from the teacher CFG-extrapolated prediction. The CFG direction |cond - uncond| is 1.03-1.13 pct of |cond| at every probed timestep, so the objective prices continuous-w direction at roughly one percent of the signal. Unfreezing the embedding made the response large; it did not make the objective supervise its direction.

sentinel_cosine.note: measured at ddim index 2; v4 is far above the collapsed band but did not beat v2 on direction

sentinel_magnitude_ratio.note: v4 IS closer to the theoretical sentinel magnitude than v2

w_conditioning_outcome.v2_comparability_caveat: v2's continuous-w cosines are computed on a response of ~0.003 against ref_l2 ~75 (3.7e-5 relative), which is noise-level; a cosine on a noise-level response is itself noise, so v2's numbers are not a meaningful comparison point.
w_conditioning_outcome.verdict: NOT ACHIEVED. The run trained cleanly and matched v2 on teacher fidelity, but continuous-w direction never consolidated, so cfg.w remains decorative and only the w=-1 sentinel works -- the same standing as v2.
w_conditioning_outcome.w4_caveat: w=4 is twice the distilled ceiling w_max=2.0, so its near-zero cosine is extrapolation. w=0 and w=2 are in-distribution, and w=2 turning negative is the substantive finding.

conclusion: Completed: 8/8 shards fail=0, merge exit 0, 5 h 18 m wall (13:25:40-18:43:54 local) against a 4.99 h precedent. All 20 merge anchors held: sequence_count 375, scene_count 26, window sum 2271, merged_shard_count 8, canonical ordinals 0..374 complete with no duplicates, excluded_as_warmup 5 (canonical not shard-local), zero non-finite episodes, key set identical to the C gate, timing_valid false with the contention reason, RDS unavailable, checkpoint sha 5daaf813, schema_version 4. THE SEAM GAP IS NOT INHERITED FROM THE DIFFUSION TEACHER, AND DISTILLATION IMPROVES IT. Paired sequence-level bootstrap, 10,000 replicates, seed 42, 375 paired episodes, harness validated by an identity self-test plus a positive control that reproduces every published c_guided_v4 vs-GT ratio to the printed digit. boundary_jerk: B v2 222.498 = 2.64x GT (84.439), C v2 159.020 = 1.88x, B->C -63.554 CI [-82.501, -46.372] SIG; distillation removes 46% of B's excess over GT. jerk_ratio B 1.92x, C 1.82x, delta -0.118 CI [-0.211, -0.026] SIG. interior_jerk is the sharper finding: B v2 22.007 above GT CI [15.835, 28.596] SIG at 1.31x, while C v2 is 0.97x and NOT significantly different from GT -- so distillation does not merely reduce the seam, it takes interior smoothness from significantly-worse-than-GT to GT parity (-23.830 CI [-29.599, -18.629] SIG). transition_distance_aligned, the rotation-invariant control, agrees: B 1.44x SIG worse than GT on interactive, C 1.17x; so B's deficit is partly positional, not only third-derivative jitter. fs_nemf B 1.22x vs C 1.12x, B->C -0.024 SIG, and NON-VACUOUS this time (0/375 exact zeros in B, C and GT alike, against 208/375 pre-repair). Scene interaction and goal reaching are essentially unchanged by distillation: pen_ratio, pen_depth_mean, pene_pct_scene, pene_sum_mean_floorexcl, contact_count, skate_ratio, success_last_10cm and success_min_10cm all ns on the B->C delta, and success_min_10cm is exactly 1.0000 for both. B is significantly WORSE than C on goal_planar_err_m (0.0851 vs 0.0610 m, SIG) and last_dist (0.0337 vs 0.0284 m, SIG). STRATIFIED (walk 130 / interactive 245, discriminator caption==walk): the direction holds in both but the magnitude does not. walk B 1.70x -> C 1.29x, distillation removing 59% of the excess; interactive B 3.26x -> C 2.28x, removing 43%, and interactive jerk_ratio B->C is ns. So interactive motion remains the deficit stratum in BOTH models, and B is the worse of the two there. SUPERSESSION, registered here because the registry is append-only and old rows are never mutated: all model-side geometric numbers in p1-hsi-b-eval-epoch222-shard8-s42-20260816 and p1-hsi-b-eval-epoch222-unguided-shard8-s42-20260816 are PRE-representation-repair, must not be used for current decisions, and must not appear in any table alongside a post-repair row. Their provenance, cost and protocol conclusions (window-balanced sharding, timing nulling, RDS gating) remain valid and are still cited; this row's own 4.99 h cost figure is taken from the guided one, which is legitimate because it is wall clock, not geometry. Their output directories b_guided_shard8 and b_unguided_shard8 were neither overwritten nor reused.

config.content:
defaults:
  - _self_
  - dataset: lingo_v3_test
  - guidance:
      - pelvis
  - model:
      - infbagel
  - sampler:
      - pelvis

exp_name: lingo-hsi-eval
seed: 42
train: false
batch_size: 1
device: cuda:0
vis: false
start_type: stand

max_window_size: 16
auto_regre_num: 2
interp_s: 3
fps: 30.0

load_language: true
load_scene: true
load_scene_goal: true
load_pelvis_goal: true
load_object_goal: true
use_pi: true
use_random_frame_bps: false
use_object_keypoints: false
# Keep the sampler's shape-only object tensor alive for its settled occ_temp
# interface. The scene-only dataset wrapper never writes it into occupancy.
add_object_voxel: true

human_only_ratio: 0.4
lingo_scene_num: 111
lingo_data_ratio: 1.0
empty_omomo_scene: false
random_seed: 42

scene_type: occ_temp
temp_voxel_num: 3
w: 1
guidance_weight: 1
use_guidance: false
sample_type: consistency
timing_warmup_sequences: 5

# Opt-in motion export.  When false nothing is written beyond
# evaluation/per_sequence_metrics.json and that payload carries no
# motion_export key, so an export-capable build reproduces a pre-export payload
# byte for byte.  When true, motion/<sequence_id>.npz is written next to it with
# global_jpos at the rollout rate (fps = fps / interp_s) for the frozen
# text-motion evaluator, plus the SMPL-X FK inputs so a later metric
# redefinition is a CPU rebuild instead of another GPU run.
export_motion: false

lingo_hsi_mode: ground_truth
lingo_sequence_limit: null

# Episode sharding for the quality pass.  shard_count=1 is the serial protocol
# and is the default; >1 splits the canonical episode enumeration by greedy
# longest-first bin packing over per-episode window counts, and invalidates
# every timing aggregate because the shards contend for the host.
# 2026-08-20 diagnostic gate, default OFF so the sealed path is bitwise unchanged.
# test_infbagel_hosi.sample_step zeroes `pi` inside `if is_loco:` but leaves `end_pi`,
# so the model receives end_pi - pi = 42*step + 48 while training carries
# min(pi + 16*3, seq_len) i.e. exactly 48 on 517,484 of 529,132 need_pi windows.
# Only step 0 is training-legal: 375 of 2271 eval windows (16.5%).
# true = keep the true pi, restoring end_pi - pi == 48 on every window.
hsi_progress_fix: false

# 2026-08-20 diagnostic gates on the per-window pelvis goal, both default to the
# CURRENT behaviour so every sealed cell stays bitwise reproducible.
#
# Training (datasets/infbagel.py:468-477) feeds pelvis_goal = joints[w0+45, 0] with
# y=0 for both the sit/lie and loco branches -- a per-window target.  The driver
# instead takes a point `hsi_lookahead_m` ahead along _straight_trajectory(), a
# straight chord from episode start to episode goal.  Measured distance from the
# driver's choice to training's target, over all 2271 windows:
#   walk 1099 windows: 1.0180 m mean (straight chord) vs 0.2124 m (GT pelvis path)
#   sit/lie 609      : 0.2012 m                       vs 0.1643 m
# and the GT pelvis advances only 0.478 m (walk) / 0.186 m (sit/lie) over those 45
# raw frames, against a hardcoded 0.8 m.  On a real wiggly path 0.8 m of ARC length
# nets ~0.48 m of displacement, so the constant is arc-length-calibrated; the chord
# makes arc length equal displacement, so it overshoots ~1.7x on walk.
# Evidence: .claude/scratch/isloco_offline_20260820/{goal_source_error.py,controls.py}
#
# hsi_gt_trajectory: true = build the lookahead path from the episode's GROUND-TRUTH
#   pelvis xz path instead of the chord.  Attribution UPPER BOUND only -- it feeds
#   privileged information a deployment cannot have.  Never use it for a baseline.
hsi_gt_trajectory: false
# hsi_lookahead_m: the lookahead arc length in metres.  0.8 is the released value.
#   0.48 is the deployable variant: one global constant, no privileged information.
hsi_lookahead_m: 0.8

shard_index: 0
shard_count: 1

# Serial latency pass.  Selects a deterministic scene-spanning episode subset
# sized by window budget; requires shard_count=1 so timing stays valid.
# 70 windows = 19 episodes over 18 of the 26 scenes; after the 5 warmup episodes
# that leaves 48 timed windows, i.e. ~47 min of measured guided-diffusion
# sampling at the measured 59.1 s/window (~68 min of total run wall clock).
latency_subset: false
latency_target_windows: 70

# lingo_hsi_mode=merge_shards inputs.  merge_shard_dir defaults to the parent
# directory the sharded runs wrote into; the expected totals are the full
# protocol and are the external anchor against a silently short merge.
merge_shard_dir: null
merge_expected_episodes: 375
merge_expected_windows: 2271
# 2026-08-18: default moved from `data/lingo_hsi_test/data` (v1) to v2. In v1
# `pelvis_goal` was the last frame of the FIRST 16-frame window, held fixed for
# the whole rollout, so start->goal was <= 0.778 m over all 375 episodes and the
# 0.8 m lookahead in `sample_step` clamped on every window of every episode
# (measured 0/2271 unclamped). v2 sets the goal to the rollout terminus; GT then
# scores `last_dist` == 0. The four sealed model cells and every
# `results/lingo_hsi/ground_truth*` row except `ground-truth-v2`/`-v3` predate
# this and were run against v1 -- reproduce those with an explicit
# `lingo_episode_dir=${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/data/lingo_hsi_test/data` override.
lingo_episode_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/data/lingo_hsi_test_v2/data
lingo_mesh_root: /data/yujinlun/datasets/LINGO/Scene_mesh
lingo_output_dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/results/lingo_hsi/${lingo_hsi_mode}-${sample_type}-${oc.select:use_guidance,false}
ckpt_path: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/checkpoint/checkpoint.pth
# When null, the evaluator uses the checkpoint file stem.
model_name: null
smplx_batch_size: 128

hydra:
  run:
    dir: ${oc.env:ROOT_DIR}/.claude/scratch/hydra_lingo_hsi

hypothesis: First evaluation of the POST-REPAIR full diffusion teacher hsi_b_lingo_full_v2_epoch222 (sha 5daaf813, bit-identical to the teacher C v2 and C v4 were distilled from), guided, on the LINGO v3 test protocol, 375 episodes / 2271 windows, 8-way sharded. Purpose: the only B evaluations on record scored the PRE-repair checkpoint at commit 101ac84, which predates the representation repair 3ded4eb + a4c979c (2026-08-18), so every model-side geometric number in them is invalid and the B->C delta was unmeasured. Without it the residual seam gap (boundary_jerk, jerk_ratio) cannot be attributed to the diffusion teacher versus the consistency distillation. Protocol is item-for-item the C v2 guided gate row p1-hsi-c-v2-eval-epoch089-guided-progressfix-s42-20260821 with sample_type flipped to diffusion, including hsi_progress_fix=true; sharding verified bitwise-neutral at 500 steps (141/141 identical) against three negative controls that do fail.
next_action: The user's question that motivated this run is answered, and the answer inverts the premise: fixing the distillation to read the diffusion model's problems through it is not viable, because distillation is not seam-transparent -- it removes 46% of B's boundary_jerk excess and lifts interior_jerk from SIG-worse-than-GT to parity. Any C-only reading therefore FLATTERS the teacher. The corollary is that the outstanding seam work is diffusion-side, not CM-side: B v2 at 2.64x GT (interactive 3.26x) is the larger defect, and C is the better model on every jerk metric. Do not read this as licence to stop distilling. Per the user's instruction this run was guided only: do NOT auto-start the unguided pass, do not modify B or C, do not add a continuous-w loss, do not retrain. The continuous-w line stays deferred pending the user's decision on this attribution. Also still open and unchanged: the Phase 1C gate threshold is the user's to set; loss_w_fk 3 is measured far better than 50 but is not derived-optimal; and the pelvis up-axis p95 residual and the non-rigid joint channel remain unaddressed on both experts.

global_jpos.note: dataset channel order, no re-indexing and no SMPL-X FK; slots 24-27 are SMPL-X 25/34/40/49 (index1/ring1) as in the frozen evaluator's training bundle, not SMPLX_JOINTS_28's middle1

motion_export.layout: one non-pickle NPZ per sequence under motion/<sequence_id>.npz

smplx.note: schema 2 onward both arms share one SMPL-X parameter frame -- the frame human_joints_aligned.npy is stored in -- and smplx_output_transform is always 'identity', so the rebuild above needs no per-arm branch; a schema-1 generated-arm file instead needs transl replaced by zup_to_yup(transl) and its recorded 'zup_to_yup' output transform ignored
smplx.rebuild: pose = concatenate([global_orient[:, None], body_pose], axis=1); vertices, joints28 = run_smplx_model(pose, transl, betas, gender, joints_ind=SMPLX_JOINTS_28).  Wrap with StitchedSequence(frames, seams=seams*interp_scale, window_lengths=window_lengths*interp_scale, history_frames=history_frames*interp_scale) to recompute seam metrics.

rds.skipped_reason: guidance pulls joints toward free voxels regardless of need_scene, so a guided null-scene rollout is confounded; RDS is scoped to unguided cells

timing.timing_invalid_reason: shard_count>1: concurrent shards contend for host CPU, PCIe and the SDF cache, so every wall-clock aggregate is contaminated; FPS comes only from a serial latency_subset pass

conclusion: Completed: 8/8 shards fail=0, merge exit 0, 2 h 39 m wall (02:26:26-05:05:26 local), all 20 merge anchors held including excluded_as_warmup 5 and a key set identical to the guided cells. GUIDANCE IS THE JERK SOURCE IN B, NOT THE SAMPLER. Removing guidance at fixed model: boundary_jerk 222.498 -> 127.924, delta -94.574 CI [-116.624, -74.930] SIG, i.e. 2.64x GT -> 1.51x; interior_jerk 92.383 -> 63.717, delta -28.666 SIG, 1.31x GT -> 0.90x, which is BELOW GT; jerk_ratio 2.295 -> 2.030 SIG. The mechanism named on 2026-08-23 is fully accounted for: episodes with any root-acceleration frame above 5g go 31/375 -> 0/375 and the total count of such frames 132 -> 0; frames above 2g per episode 1.355 -> 0.019; mean per-episode max root acceleration 19.68 -> 8.84 m/s^2, delta -10.84 CI [-13.48, -8.47] SIG; walk episodes whose pelvis dips below 0.6 m go 13/130 -> 0/130. Root jerk at the boundary 142.18 -> 59.75, delta -82.42 SIG. Guidance raises the boundary more than the interior (excess ratio 1.200 CI [1.124, 1.278]), so it is a per-step process with extra bite at the seam rather than a purely uniform elevation, which refines the 08-23 uniform-offset reading. THE TRADE IS REAL AND EXPECTED: without guidance penetration degrades, pen_ratio 0.0255 -> 0.0354 (0.91x GT -> 1.26x), pene_pct_scene 0.0523 -> 0.0608, pen_depth_mean 0.0526 -> 0.0548, contact_count 893 -> 943, all SIG; min_dist falls 0.0048 -> 0.0030 so the body sits closer to surfaces. Goal reaching IMPROVES unguided: goal_planar_err_m 0.0851 -> 0.0516 m and last_dist 0.0337 -> 0.0235 m, both SIG, and success_min_10cm stays exactly 1.0000. RDS = 0.14650 CI [0.13930, 0.15385], median 0.13328, p10 0.06789, p90 0.24519, with 0 of 375 episodes below 0.005: B GENUINELY USES THE SCENE, it is not ignoring the conditioning. B's RDS is significantly higher than C's, +0.01535 CI [+0.00954, +0.02115].

use_object_keypoints: false

# Opt-in motion export.  When false nothing is written beyond
# evaluation/per_sequence_metrics.json and that payload carries no
# motion_export key, so an export-capable build reproduces a pre-export payload
# byte for byte.  When true, motion/<sequence_id>.npz is written next to it with
# global_jpos at the rollout rate (fps = fps / interp_s) for the frozen
# text-motion evaluator, plus the SMPL-X FK inputs so a later metric
# redefinition is a CPU rebuild instead of another GPU run.
export_motion: false

lingo_hsi_mode: ground_truth
lingo_sequence_limit: null

# Episode sharding for the quality pass.  shard_count=1 is the serial protocol
# and is the default; >1 splits the canonical episode enumeration by greedy
# longest-first bin packing over per-episode window counts, and invalidates
# every timing aggregate because the shards contend for the host.
# 2026-08-20 diagnostic gate, default OFF so the sealed path is bitwise unchanged.
# test_infbagel_hosi.sample_step zeroes `pi` inside `if is_loco:` but leaves `end_pi`,
# so the model receives end_pi - pi = 42*step + 48 while training carries
# min(pi + 16*3, seq_len) i.e. exactly 48 on 517,484 of 529,132 need_pi windows.
# Only step 0 is training-legal: 375 of 2271 eval windows (16.5%).
# true = keep the true pi, restoring end_pi - pi == 48 on every window.
hsi_progress_fix: false

# hsi_guidance_norm_cap: per-step trust region on the guidance increment, applied on
# the DIFFUSION path only (Sampler.p_sample); the consistency path is untouched.
# null = off, and the arithmetic emitted is byte-identical to the released path -- no
# norm is computed and no extra tensor op runs.  A float caps the increment's PER-SAMPLE
# L2 norm: gradient *= min(1, cap / (||gradient|| + 1e-12)).
# It exists because the matched 2x2 of 2026-08-23 attributed 100% of the physically
# impossible root accelerations to guidance -- 132 frames over 5g in B v2 guided and 41
# in C v2 guided against 0 in both unguided cells -- and 80.2% of the summed effect
# magnitude on boundary_jerk to guidance-involving terms, with the interaction (64.401)
# the largest single term.  The released sampler adds the increment unnormalised once
# per sampler step, 499 times per window against the consistency path's 16.
# Units are those of the normalised 232-channel x_start, so a threshold is only
# meaningful relative to a measured increment distribution; see
# docs/plan/PHASE_1C_HSI.md 2026-08-23 SS-H.
hsi_guidance_norm_cap: null

# The two DOSE knobs, both off by default and both diffusion-path only.  They exist
# because the 2026-08-23 norm-cap smoke measured the per-step increment distributions and
# found the magnitude hypothesis false: B's increments are SMALLER than C's at every
# percentile up to p99 (p50 0.688x, mean 0.717x), and larger only at the extreme max.
# What differs is the count -- guidance fires on every step but the last, so 499 times per
# window on the diffusion path against 15 on the consistency path, giving 23.8x the total
# per-window displacement (499 x 46.54 = 23,225 against 15 x 64.94 = 974).
#
# hsi_guidance_dose_scale: a constant multiplier on the increment.  null = off.  1/23.8 =
# 0.04202 makes B's per-window total displacement equal C's, measured 975.8 vs C's 974.1.
#
# hsi_guidance_alpha_decay: multiply the increment by (1 - alpha_cumprod_t), the factor
# written and then commented out at the consistency-path guidance site.  alpha_cumprod
# rises to 1 as t falls to 0, so this SUPPRESSES guidance on the late low-noise refinement
# steps and keeps it on the early high-noise ones.  It is not equivalent to a constant
# scale: measured on the frozen worst-20 it takes the per-window total to 0.596x, i.e.
# 14.21x C rather than 23.84x, so it is a partial dose reduction with a schedule shape.
hsi_guidance_dose_scale: null
hsi_guidance_alpha_decay: false

# 2026-08-20 diagnostic gates on the per-window pelvis goal, both default to the
# CURRENT behaviour so every sealed cell stays bitwise reproducible.
#
# Training (datasets/infbagel.py:468-477) feeds pelvis_goal = joints[w0+45, 0] with
# y=0 for both the sit/lie and loco branches -- a per-window target.  The driver
# instead takes a point `hsi_lookahead_m` ahead along _straight_trajectory(), a
# straight chord from episode start to episode goal.  Measured distance from the
# driver's choice to training's target, over all 2271 windows:
#   walk 1099 windows: 1.0180 m mean (straight chord) vs 0.2124 m (GT pelvis path)
#   sit/lie 609      : 0.2012 m                       vs 0.1643 m
# and the GT pelvis advances only 0.478 m (walk) / 0.186 m (sit/lie) over those 45
# raw frames, against a hardcoded 0.8 m.  On a real wiggly path 0.8 m of ARC length
# nets ~0.48 m of displacement, so the constant is arc-length-calibrated; the chord
# makes arc length equal displacement, so it overshoots ~1.7x on walk.
# Evidence: .claude/scratch/isloco_offline_20260820/{goal_source_error.py,controls.py}
#
# hsi_gt_trajectory: true = build the lookahead path from the episode's GROUND-TRUTH
#   pelvis xz path instead of the chord.  Attribution UPPER BOUND only -- it feeds
#   privileged information a deployment cannot have.  Never use it for a baseline.
hsi_gt_trajectory: false
# hsi_lookahead_m: the lookahead arc length in metres.  0.8 is the released value.
#   0.48 is the deployable variant: one global constant, no privileged information.
hsi_lookahead_m: 0.8

shard_index: 0

# Serial latency pass.  Selects a deterministic scene-spanning episode subset
# sized by window budget; requires shard_count=1 so timing stays valid.

# P16-NS -- model B retrained from scratch with the training-time need_scene gate
# forced ON.  ONE manipulated variable against config_train_hsi_b_lingo_full.
#
# THE VARIABLE.  The released LINGO pickle
# data/dataset/language_motion_dict/language_motion_dict__inter_and_loco__16.pkl
# carries a precomputed per-window `need_scene` boolean.  On the 1,343,667 v3
# training windows it is False on 522,818 of them (38.9098%), and
# models/infbagel.py:1433-1438 zeroes all five scene tokens -- scene_emb, the
# goal-centred crop, and scene_emb_0..3 -- for exactly those rows.  Zeroing an
# activation zeroes its gradient, so under B-v2 the scene encoder was trained on
# 61.09% of rows.  Inference never reads the flag:
# test_infbagel_lingo_hsi.py:1362 pins it True for all 375 sealed episodes.  So
# 88 of the 375 gate episodes are sampled with five live scene tokens under a
# caption whose whole training history was scene-blind.  This arm removes that
# train/test conditioning mismatch and nothing else.
#
# WHAT THE FLAG DOES NOT TOUCH.  The 10% per-sample temporal-voxel dropout
# (models/infbagel.py:1401-1403) and the cfg_scale == -1 uncond mask (:1394-1399)
# both survive unchanged; they only reach scene_emb_1..3.  need_scene=False is
# the only mechanism in the codebase that also zeroes scene_emb and scene_emb_0,
# so disabling it does not leave the model without scene regularization.  The
# inference-side RDS null-scene pass is also implemented as need_scene=False
# (test_infbagel_lingo_hsi.py:1848) and is a runtime argument, not this flag.
#
# FROM SCRATCH, NOT A FINE-TUNE.  Inherited unchanged: load_state_dict false,
# ckpt_path "", resume_from "", start_epoch 0.  The baseline B-v2 is itself a
# cold start, so a warm-started arm would differ from its own baseline in total
# updates seen, in optimizer state at t=0 and in learning-rate schedule position
# -- three variables, not one.  A continuation would also have to either replay
# the 2000-update warmup into a converged model or skip it; there is no null
# choice.  And hsi_b_lingo_full_v2_resume.pth carries Adam moments fitted to the
# scene-blind regime, which is the exact state this arm exists to unlearn.

manipulated_variable.mechanism: The released LINGO pickle carries a per-window need_scene boolean that is False on 522,818 of 1,343,667 v3 training windows (38.9098%); when False the model zeroes the five scene tokens.  Forcing it True removes that train/test conditioning mismatch.

results.metrics_note: Training workload only.  No rollout or native-domain metric is claimed by this record.  The preregistered evaluation is NSu (unguided) first, with NSg only if NSu's staged trigger fires.

objective_weights.loss_w_obj_pts_inert_reason: Under lingo_only every sample takes the no-object branch, so mask_points is empty and loss_object is None.
